backend_tool:dxf_measure.description:
Measure a DXF drawing of this project, above all a Katasterauszug (BEV Katastralmappe): the site as geometry, not as a picture. Use it for questions about parcels and what stands on them: a parcel's area and shape, which parcels border it and along how much boundary, the buildings on it with their footprint and coverage, how far each building stands from each boundary, what remains buildable after setbacks you give, and what a coverage or density limit allows. For any other DXF it finds labels and says what each layer holds.

operation:
  'overview'  — what the drawing is (Katastralmappe or not, KG, coordinate system, unit), how many parcels and buildings, its layers. Start here once per file.
  'parcels'   — every parcel as a row (KG, cadastre, area, built-up area and coverage, neighbours); `parcels` names some.
  'parcel'    — one parcel (`parcel`): area, perimeter, enclosing rectangle, boundary length per neighbour and to the edge of the extract, the buildings on it.
  'setbacks'  — for each building on the parcel, its shortest distance to each neighbour's boundary.
  'buildable' — the parcel minus a band along each boundary: `setback_m` for every side, `setbacks` ({neighbour parcel: metres}) per side; `coverage_limit` (0.4 or 40 for 40 %) and `density_limit` (a floor-area ratio such as 1.2) as allowances. The values are the ones YOU pass, from the Bebauungsplan or the building code (look them up first); the drawing holds none.
  'distance'  — the shortest distance between two things in `between`: parcel numbers or 'building N'.
  'texts'     — labels containing `query`, with their layer, position and parcel.
  'layers'    — what each layer holds: entity kinds, line length, closed outlines and their area.

`document` is the file name as the inventory lists it; empty means the document open on the canvas or the conversation's subject. Name parcels as the drawing does ('123/4', '.57'). Every answer says how far it can be trusted: Grundsteuerkataster boundaries are graphic and not legally binding, so quote that caveat with the number. 'Undecidable' is an answer about the file: report what is missing and the remedy. Never recompute, round or convert a returned number.

schema.description: What the model passes to ``dxf_measure``.

between.description: Two parcel numbers or 'building N', for 'distance'.
between.title: Between

building_layers.description: Layers holding building outlines, for a DXF that is not a cadastral map.
building_layers.title: Building Layers

document.description: The DXF's file name; empty for the open document or the subject.
document.title: Document

query.description: Text to find with 'texts'; empty lists every label.
query.title: Query

setbacks.description: Setback per neighbouring parcel number, metres; overrides setback_m there.
setbacks.title: Setbacks

schema.title: DxfMeasureInput

backend_tool:ifc_measure.description:
MEASURE the project's IFC/BIM model — geometry, topology and spatial relationships — and report every number with the provenance it came with. Use this when the answer is a DIMENSION, a DISTANCE, an AREA the export may not have published, or a spatial relationship ('which room does this window open into', 'wie hoch ist der Raum wirklich', 'wie weit ist die Tür von der Wand', 'welche Bauteile begrenzen diesen Raum').

This is NOT a replacement for ifc_query. ifc_query reads the extracted index: it is fast, it covers the whole model, and it answers what the export WROTE DOWN — counts, storeys, property values, published quantities. Reach for it first for 'how many' and 'which ones'. Reach for ifc_measure when the file does not state the number and the geometry has to be read, or when a declared number needs a second, independent route to check it against.

CALL 'briefing' FIRST, once per model, before anything else. The briefing is this FILE speaking: it names the storeys with their elevations, the property vocabulary this exporter actually used (DIALEKT), and — the part that saves whole turns — the BLIND section, which says which questions this file cannot answer at all. Storey and property names come from THERE, copied verbatim. A storey name you invented matches nothing, and an empty result reads like 'the building has none'.

What each operation is FOR (the parameters say which arguments it takes):
  'briefing'       — this file speaking about itself. START HERE.
  'find_elements'  — GlobalIds by type, name, storey or spatial role. The input every other operation needs.
  'element'        — everything about ONE element, including which relations it actually has, so a relation that would come back empty need not be guessed at.
  'relations'      — one topological question about one element.
  'measure'        — one measurement of one element, or of an already-known set of them.
  'survey'         — ONE measure across ALL elements of a selection, each named, with the SPREAD over the set. Reach for this the moment the question is plural — 'wie hoch ist der Keller' names one room and means seventeen. Measuring one element and generalising is a guess. The spread IS the finding; report it.
  'element_profile' — the reverse: EVERY measure that applies to ONE element, in one call. Which measures apply follows from the element's IFC type, so a door is not asked for its lichte Raumhöhe. Reach for it once an element has become interesting, such as the outlier a survey named.
  'distance'       — the distance between TWO elements, along an axis, between centroids or boxes. An Achsabstand, never a clear dimension.
  'clearance'      — the LICHTE dimension between TWO elements: the smallest SURFACE-to-SURFACE gap, which 'distance' does not have: its 'min' is a gap between BOUNDING BOXES, a lower bound that lets too tight pass as free. For the clear width of ONE opening use 'measure' with clearWidth instead.
  'sun_position'   — where the sun stood over this building at an instant: azimuth, altitude, and the direction TOWARDS the sun in THIS model's coordinates. NOT a Besonnungsstudie: it says where the sun was, never whether the neighbour's gable was in the way — that needs everything outside the property line, which is not in the file. Undecidable without IfcSite.RefLatitude/RefLongitude; no latitude is assumed, so it takes no coordinates.
  'storey_heights' — the storey pitch (slab top to slab top) for every storey. This is the STRUCTURAL height, NOT the lichte Raumhöhe (that is measure/clearHeight).
  'room_inventory' — rooms grouped by a SUSPECTED use, inferred from their names. A proposal for a human to confirm, never a finding.
  'fire'           — the OIB 2 (Brandschutz) geometry. NO Gebäudeklasse: escape_level returns a HEIGHT, and which class follows from it is a legal classification under OIB 2 plus Landesrecht.
  'envelope'       — the OIB 6 (Wärmeschutz) geometry of the WHOLE building. Asking wall by wall is how the wall that was left out stays invisible, so it takes no element. No U-value is CALCULATED: a declared one is repeated, a missing one stays missing, never derived from the layer set. Costs geometry (seconds).
  'overhang'       — how far one element projects past another's facade plane. The Dachüberstand, the balcony, the canopy.
  'light_incidence' — builds the light prism over an opening's lower edge and reports which elements reach into it and how deep. The result is GEOMETRY: a cut prism enlarges the required Lichteintrittsfläche under OIB 3, it does not ban the window. Report what intrudes and how far, then apply the clause yourself. The host wall is deliberately not excluded on its own, because a window set deep in a thick wall genuinely is shaded by its own reveal — but if the wall comes back as an obstruction, re-run with it excluded (keeping any other exclusion) and say so.
  'view'           — LOOK at a floor plan. Returns the storey as an IMAGE you can actually see, cut at 1.2 m so door and window openings appear as gaps. Use it to settle which element is meant, to sanity-check that a measured arrangement looks the way the numbers imply, or before measuring at all. ~6 s.
  'draw'           — the same floor plan as an SVG FILE for the USER (~5 s). It returns a path, not an image: you cannot see it. Use 'view' when YOU need to look, 'draw' when the user wants the file.
  'shopping_list'  — writes the model's blind spots as a buildingSMART IDS 1.0 file the architect can run in Solibri/BIMcollab/ifctester against their own model. Offer it when several answers came back undecidable, or when asked what to fix in the export. It requires only that a property EXISTS, never its value. The summary names the blind spots it could not express.

PROVENANCE — the reason this tool exists. Every answer says HOW it was obtained, and the three are three different sentences in German that must not be swapped:
  'declared' → „laut Modell …“ / „das Modell deklariert …“. The file states it.
  'computed' → „gemessen: … (±Toleranz)“. WE measured it from the geometry. The tolerance is part of the claim — quote it. NEVER write a computed number as something the model states.
  'inferred' → „vermutlich …“ plus the reasons. A heuristic, offered for confirmation, never a finding. room_inventory is always this: whether a room is an Aufenthaltsraum is a LEGAL classification, not a geometric one.
The rendered summary line already carries the right verb — quote that line rather than reassembling the claim yourself.

'decidable: false' is NOT an error and NOT a fact about the building. It means the question was well formed and THIS EXPORT cannot answer it. Report it as a finding about the export, name what is missing, and pass on 'missing.remedy' verbatim — that sentence is what the architect changes in their CAD to make the question answerable. Saying 'the building has no sill height' when the file merely does not publish one is a wrong answer.

NEVER recompute, round, convert or extrapolate a number this tool returns. Do not add two areas together, do not derive a third dimension from two others, do not restate a millimetre value in centimetres. If a question needs a number that was not returned, make another call — arithmetic done in an answer is a guess wearing the tool's authority. And NEVER read a measurement off a drawing ('view' or 'draw'): a value read off an image is guessed even when it happens to be right.

COST — plan the calls before making them. 'briefing', 'find_elements' and 'element' are free (pure topology). The first 'measure' or 'distance' on a model tessellates it (~2 s for a single-family house). The relations marked [geometry] cost seconds on a cold model: opensTo, bounds, enclosedBy and adjacentSpaces build a space-contact map on first use (about 7 s), because most exports write no IfcRelSpaceBoundary. After that everything is milliseconds. Do NOT call the geometric relations speculatively — call them when the answer needs them.

A typical chain ('ist die Raumhöhe im Wohnzimmer ausreichend?'): operation='briefing'; operation='find_elements' ifc_type='IfcSpace' name_contains='Wohn' storey='<from the briefing>'; operation='measure' measure='clearHeight' on that GlobalId, or operation='survey' on the whole storey; report the rendered line as it stands.

When the model cannot be resolved the tool says so in German — report that sentence rather than answering from your own knowledge of buildings.

A measurement that contradicts a declared quantity is reported as a contradiction ('Widerspruch'), and that is a FINDING an architect wants before submission: their schedule and their geometry disagree. Report both numbers and which one the tool preferred; do not silently pick one.

schema.description: The arguments of one ``ifc_measure`` call, as the model sees them.

angle_deg.description: 'light_incidence' only — the Lichteinfallswinkel in degrees, strictly between 0 and 90. It is a fact about the BESTIMMUNG, not the model (OIB 3: 45, with swivel_deg 30), so the tool refuses without it rather than defaulting.
angle_deg.title: Angle Deg

global_id.description: The element's IFC GlobalId, from 'find_elements', 'element' or an ifc_query result in THIS turn; an invented id is refused. Usually ONE id. A list (or one comma-separated string) where the question is about a set: 'measure' over an already-known selection (at most 50, each element keeping its own answer, tolerance and refusal), 'view' to mark several at once, 'fire' with kind='compartmentArea' for the rooms of the compartment, exactly two rooms for kind='separatingElements'. The selecting and whole-model operations ('find_elements', 'survey', 'draw', 'envelope') take none.
global_id.title: Global Id

ifc_type.description: 'find_elements', 'survey' and 'draw' — the IFC CLASS, e.g. IfcSpace, IfcWindow, IfcDoor. The spatial role goes in 'kind' instead.
ifc_type.title: Ifc Type

kind.description:
Three vocabularies on one field, scoped by operation.
  'find_elements' and 'survey' — the spatial ROLE, not the IFC type (a room is 'space'): project, site, building, storey, space, element, opening, group.
  'fire' — which OIB 2 (Brandschutz) geometry, default 'escape_level':
    escape_level — height of the topmost occupied floor above the lowest adjoining ground — the number the Gebäudeklasse hangs on. Returns a HEIGHT and never a class
    compartmentArea — floor area of a fire compartment across several rooms, each room listed
    separatingElements — what lies BETWEEN two rooms — wall, slab, and the doors in them — each with its DECLARED FireRating, and explicitly with its absence
    siteBoundary — distance to the site boundary (Brandübertragung). Undecidable on most exports, because a parcel boundary is rarely exported — and it is not guessed here
    doorGraph — the WHOLE building's walkable graph: rooms as nodes, OUTSIDE as its own node, doors as edges, plus the doors that became NEITHER (unbestimmt, ausgeschlossen). A room with no edge has no way out; an unresolved door is a hole in every route. Takes no global_id
  'envelope' — which OIB 6 (Wärmeschutz) geometry of the WHOLE building, default 'thermalEnvelope':
    thermalEnvelope — which elements form the boundary between heated inside and outside, grouped by kind, each with its area, its DECLARED U-value and which rung decided it (declared IsExternal or inferred from room contact), plus interior (decided, left out) and unbestimmt (neither counted nor discarded)
    areaByOrientation — envelope area per compass bearing, opaque and transparent apart, with the window-to-wall ratio per facade. Needs a declared TrueNorth; without one the bearing is refused, not guessed
    compactness — A/V in 1/m, with the characteristic length (V over A), and A and V separately. V is the NET volume (the sum of the IfcSpace solids)
  'element_profile' — 'expensive' to include escape route, reachability, turning circle and door approach, which are left out otherwise.
Unused by every other operation.
kind.title: Kind

limit.description: How many rows: 'find_elements' up to 500, 'survey' up to 50. 0 leaves the server's default.
limit.title: Limit

measure.description:
'measure' (one element) and 'survey' (a whole selection) — WHICH quantity:
    extent — width, depth, height and centroid of one element
    floorArea — a room's floor area FROM THE GEOMETRY, even when the export publishes none; a published one is compared and a contradiction reported
    sillAndHead — Brüstungs- und Sturzhöhe of a window/door above ITS OWN storey
    elevation — underside and top, absolute and above the element's own storey
    clearHeight — lichte Raumhöhe — floor to the LOWEST thing hanging into the room (suspended ceiling, downstand, duct). NOT the height of the space solid ('extent'), which a Raumhöhennachweis must not use
    azimuth — which way a facade faces. Undecidable without TrueNorth in the file
    lightEntryArea — a ROOM's light-entry area and what percent of its floor area that is — the number an OIB 3 daylight check comes down to. Sums only the EXTERNAL openings (an internal door lights nothing) and measures the structural clear opening, not the glazed area. Applies no threshold: the percentage is in the Bestimmung, not in the model
    egressPath — a ROOM's shortest WALKABLE route to the outside through doors (adjacency is not walkability), with the rooms, the doors and a length. The length runs through room and door centres, so it is a LOWER BOUND and not a Fluchtweglänge
    reachableFrom — every room reachable from this one through doors, with door counts. Answers 'which rooms are behind this door', and finds rooms with no way out at all — itself a finding
    clearWidth — the LICHTE Breite and Höhe of an opening, measured on the aperture itself. THIS is what a door-width or escape-route-width check needs
    orientedExtent — length/width/height along the ELEMENT's own axes plus its bearing from north. Use for anything skewed to the model grid, where 'extent' is axis-aligned and systematically too large
    roomDepth — how deep a room runs back from its daylight facade, the width along that facade, and the ratio to the clear height. Names which facade it chose and, for a corner room, the runner-up
    stairGeometry — riser height, tread depth, riser count and the NUTZBREITE of a stair flight, plus the SPREAD of the risers. Declared values are checked against the geometry and a contradiction reported
    rampSlope — a ramp's slope as a percentage AND as a ratio, with run, rise and clear width
    headroom — clear height over a stair flight or ramp, measured PERPENDICULAR to the pitch, not vertically
    stepsOf — the flights and landings a stair is made of, so one flight can be asked about
    turningCircle — the largest circle that fits on a ROOM's free floor, for a Wendekreis check. Counts fixed built-ins only; furniture is reported beside it. Applies no threshold
    thresholdHeight — the step at a door. Where the export models no floor build-up this is a STRUCTURAL number, which says nothing about the finished threshold, and the answer says so
    balustrade — where there is a fall at an opening, how far, and what stands there. Undecidable when the export contains no IfcRailing at all
    clearApproach — the free floor in front of a door on each side, and what ends it
measure.title: Measure

mode.description:
Two vocabularies on one field, scoped by operation.
  'distance' (default 'min'):
    min — gap between the two axis-aligned BOUNDING BOXES. 0 means the boxes overlap — it does NOT prove the solids touch, and on a skewed element the true gap is larger
    centroid — centre to centre in 3D (Achsabstand). NOT a clear dimension
    horizontal — centre to centre in plan, Z ignored (Achsabstand) — what a plan drawing scales off. NOT a lichte Breite: for a clear width use measure/clearWidth on the opening
    vertical — difference in centre HEIGHT — what a section scales off. NOT a lichte Höhe: for that use measure/clearHeight on the room
  NONE of those four is a clear dimension: use operation='clearance' for the smallest surface-to-surface gap.
  'view' (default 'highlight'):
    highlight — mark these elements red on the full plan — 'where is this in the building'
    only — draw nothing but these elements — 'what does this look like'
Unused by every other operation.
mode.title: Mode

model_name.description: A substring of the file name, to pick one model when the project has several. Leave it empty when there is only one.
model_name.title: Model Name

name_contains.description: 'find_elements' and 'survey' — a substring of the element's name. Take it from the briefing or from an earlier result; an invented fragment matches nothing.
name_contains.title: Name Contains

operation.description: WHICH question to ask. The only required argument — every other field is scoped by this one. On a model you have not looked at yet, 'briefing'.
operation.title: Operation

other_global_id.description: The SECOND element, and it means a different thing per operation. 'distance' and 'clearance': the element to measure against. 'overhang': the element whose outer face is the REFERENCE plane, while global_id is the projecting one (get it from relations/hostedIn on the window). 'light_incidence': the elements EXCLUDED from the test — a list, or several ids separated by commas. Unused by every other operation.
other_global_id.title: Other Global Id

relation.description:
'relations' only — which topological question to ask about global_id:
    hostedIn — which wall carries this window/door (from voids+fills)
    hosts — which openings are cut out of this element
    fillerOf — what fills this opening
    bounds — which elements bound this room  [geometry]
    enclosedBy — which rooms this element bounds  [geometry]
    opensTo — which rooms this window/door opens into  [geometry]
    connects — which elements butt onto this one
    contains — which elements sit in this storey or room
    containerOf — which storey or room this element sits in
    adjacentSpaces — which rooms border this room  [geometry]
    elementsOfStorey — every element of this storey, including those in rooms
    above — what is directly ABOVE this element or room  [geometry, rays; furniture excluded]
    below — what is directly BELOW it  [geometry, rays]
relation.title: Relation

room_kind.description: 'room_inventory' only — which SUSPECTED use to group the rooms by.
room_kind.title: Room Kind

storey.description: 'find_elements', 'survey', 'draw' and 'view' — the storey name EXACTLY as the briefing spells it.
storey.title: Storey

swivel_deg.description: 'light_incidence' only — the lateral Verschwenkung in degrees, from 0 to under 90. From the Bestimmung as well (OIB 3: 30).
swivel_deg.title: Swivel Deg

when.description: 'sun_position' only — an ISO 8601 instant WITH a time zone, e.g. '2026-06-21T12:00:00+02:00' or '2026-06-21T10:00:00Z'. A timestamp without a zone is refused rather than read as UTC.
when.title: When

schema.title: IfcMeasureInput

backend_tool:knowledge_search.description:
Searches the ingested knowledge base (the office's files and the OIB corpus) and returns quotable passages, each with a Citation key: the evidence tool. It does not put a file on screen (`surface_documents` does).
Inputs: `query`, a search query in the documents' language (topic, jurisdiction, year), not the raw user message. Narrow with `file_name=` (an indexed name from the inventory or the user; never invent one), `folder=` (a path as the inventory prints it after 'Ordner:'; includes everything filed beneath it; never invent one), `doc_class=` (Dokumentart key, e.g. oib_guideline), `title_contains=`, and `shelf=` (project, office or base; omitted, every shelf is read), or with `path=` as a hit's `Path:` line names a place, a folder or one file. `group_by="document"` (ranked search only) returns one entry per document: its best passage and how many passages of the ranked pool it held.
`match="exact"` returns EVERY passage that contains the query literally, plus a table of the matching files with count and pages, and shows a term is written nowhere. Several spellings go in one query separated by '|'; case, ä/ae, ß/ss and a line break, space or hyphen between words are matched for you; a term of two or three characters matches as a whole word only. `stemmed=true` also finds inflected forms. Per shelf it states how many documents were searched and how many matched.
`match="regex"` is the same search with a regex in Python syntax, case-insensitive, for a pattern (a Geschäftszahl `MA 37/\d{6}`, a fire door `\bT30-\d+`); `|` is then regex alternation. It needs one literal whole word or number it must contain (`37`, `T30`), or a `folder=`, `file_name=` or `doc_class=` to read in; a pattern that backtracks is refused. `context=` (0 to 3) adds the lines around every hit. A search that stops at its limit says so, and its counts are then lower bounds.
Returns: numbered passages with Source, Citation (cite this key verbatim), Dokumentart, Ordner, page and text. A query that names a Richtlinie and nothing else ('OIB 2') returns every part of it the corpus holds, each with its Geltungsbereich and Gliederung: every member is then open at the level a read of one document opens it, and what is left to open is a Punkt by number.
`conclusion=`: Optional: one line on what you are looking for, shown to the person. No effect on the result. Returns up to 16 excerpts by default (platform-configurable up to 50; the result header counts them), spread across multiple distinct documents (at most 5 per document where possible), so cross-cutting questions see every relevant Richtlinie.

backend_tool:law_lookup.description:
Answers a legal question from RIS (RIS – Rechtsinformationssystem des Bundes (OGD-RIS API v2.6)) with the actual provisions, quotable and citable: the statutes of the state and of each Bundesland, building codes among them, and court decisions. The office's uploads and the technical guidelines in the knowledge base are in knowledge_search, not here.

One call covers the whole path: it reads the address out of the question (§/Artikel, the named law, the Bundesland), takes the verified catalog pointer or searches RIS live, downloads at most two documents and cuts the provisions that answer the question out of them. No document number is passed.

Args:
    question (str): The legal question, in German, as the user means it, not a search string.
    conclusion (str): Optional. One line on what you are looking for; no effect on the call.
    jurisdiction (str): The Bundesland ("Wien", "Niederösterreich", …). When omitted it is taken from the instrument, the question, then the project's site, and the answer states which.
    instrument (str): An address: "Bauordnung für Wien", "§ 63 Bauordnung für Wien", a RIS document number or a www.ris.bka.gv.at URL. Naming a § makes the lookup deterministic: the provision is cut out by its number. Up to six in one call ("§§ 75 und 81 Bauordnung für Wien"); past six it names those it did not read.
    application (str): Only for the non-statute collections: "Vwgh"/"Vfgh"/"Justiz"/"Bvwg"/"Lvwg"/"Dsk" for case law, "BgblAuth"/"LgblAuth" for the authentic gazettes, "Begut"/"RegV" for drafts, "Erlaesse" for decrees. Empty for statute law.
    as_of (str): Optional YYYY-MM-DD: the version in force on that day (e.g. the filing day of a submission). A past day is read only from RIS version documents of that day, a miss rather than today's text; today or a later day reads today's text, and says so.

Returns:
    str: Numbered passages, each with Source, Dokumentart, Punkt, a Citation key to copy verbatim, and the provision's text. A miss says what was searched, which Bundesland was assumed and where that came from, what matched but was not read, and one concrete retry.

backend_tool:list_files.description:
Lists the reader's OWN files the way the Files pane shows them: which files exist, in which folder, of which Dokumentart, uploaded when. A deterministic listing, paged, not capped by the prompt inventory. It says which files exist, not what they say: reading or searching the documents does.
Inputs, all optional: with none, every file on Projektwissen, Büroablage and Private Sitzung, ordered by folder, after an overview of the top-level folders with file counts. `folder=` one folder and everything below it. `name_contains=` words that must all appear in the file name or title (case and umlaut spelling do not matter). `doc_class=` a Dokumentart key. `added_since=` YYYY-MM-DD. `sort=newest`. `topic=` a Thema recognised in the documents (Attika, Holzrahmenbau). `shelf=` project | office_shelf | session | base (base, the platform OIB corpus, is listed only when asked). `offset=` the next page, as the result says.
`view="tree"` (`depth=` 1-4, default 2) returns a card per folder instead of file lines: counts, Dokumentart mix, pages, dates, the current Fassung; filters apply, no paging.
`revisions_of=` a file name returns that document's whole chain of Fassungen, newest first, each with Index/Datum, upload date and what changed against the one before; every other filter is ignored. With `compare_to=` another Fassung of the chain (its file name, or "previous"), it returns what changed, page by page, in the printed text and in the reading of the drawings, with the Plankopf's Index and Stand („was hat sich zwischen Index B und C geändert“). `compare_to=` may also name any other file of the reader that is no Fassung of it („vergleiche die Raumliste mit dem Raumprogramm“): the two are then compared as two different documents, first → second. Either way, tables and lists (xlsx, csv, tables in a PDF) are compared row by row, matched by the column that identifies a row, and each deviating row names its place in both files.
Returns: a count, the subfolders, then one line per file: exact file name, title, folder, Dokumentart, page count, topics, the date a photo was taken, a Fassung mark (read from the name, or a replacement a person confirmed, with what changed), upload date, a one-line summary. An index, not a source: it is never cited, and a summary does not say what a file contains. File names are written exactly as returned; each becomes a link the reader can open.

backend_tool:look.description: Shows you a page of a document as an image; with `region=[x, y, w, h]` only that box, sharper. `document`: the file name from the inventory or from a hit's `Citation:` line, or a document id; empty means the document open on the canvas, then this chat's document. `page` starts at 1. `region` is shares of the page as shown: 0 to 1, origin top left, never pixels. `image_index` shows the embedded image a hit's `Image:` line names, at its own resolution; a hit's `Region:` line gives the numbers for the place it sits. Where something lies on a sheet is read off the image, not off the text. `question` (optional): a second reader, the office's vision model, answers it from the same crop as short lines starting `Gelesen:`, a reading of the drawing and never a measurement; a reading does not cost a look. A look's result carries its `[N]` to cite. A look that finds nothing is reported as absence in the prose, not shown as a card. At most 6 looks per turn, at most 2 of them whole pages; every result says how many are left. Fails open with a sentence saying why.

backend_tool:read_passage.description:
Opens a document by name: `document=` alone returns its OUTLINE, the document's opening passage plus a Gliederung of its top-level Punkte, and `document=` with `clause=` or `page=` returns exactly that passage. A lookup, not a search: no ranking, and it cannot find a document from a topic (`knowledge_search` does).
Inputs: `document`, the exact name or display title as the inventory or a hit printed it (e.g. 'OIB-Richtlinie 2, Ausgabe Mai 2023' or 'oib-rl_2_ausgabe_mai_2023.pdf'). `clause`, the number alone ('3.5.2', no 'Pkt.') or a table's caption ('Tabelle 3'), or for a project document what a hit's `Punkt:` line printed ('§ 4', 'Zeilen 2-41'); with `clause=`, `page=` is ignored. `page`, one page number. `pages`, a range ('4-6', at most 30 pages) in reading order without the overlap between neighbouring chunks, up to about 6k tokens; a read that stopped early ends with a `cursor` to pass back with the same `document=`.
Returns: the passages, each with Source, Citation (copy verbatim), Dokumentart, Punkt and page. The Gliederung is an index, not evidence: only passages carry a Citation; a Punkt it lists, or one an outline in a `knowledge_search` result lists, opens here by its number (`clause=`). An unknown document name is refused, with up to three labelled guesses from this turn's readable inventory when anything is close.
`conclusion=` is optional: one line on what you are looking for; it has no effect on the call.

of the Richtlinie. The VERDICT is not: the renderer compares its own
computed result against this and colours the card accordingly, so a card

CalculationOperand.description:
One number entering a step of the derivation, with where it came from.

Either a literal ``value`` or a reference to an earlier ``step`` — never
both, because a stated value beside a reference is two answers to the same
question and the renderer would have to pick one.

Carries the same provenance vocabulary as :class:`DimensionCheck`, for the
same reason: a derived number is only as honest as its inputs, and a
Schrittmaß computed from a measurement of ours is our claim, not the
architect's. The renderer propagates every band it is given into the result,
so a tolerance dropped here is a tolerance dropped from the answer.

factor.description: Only on a 'sum': the RULE's own multiplier for this term, e.g. 2 for a two-sided Abstand. Negative subtracts the term. Omit for a plain +1 — never use it to smuggle a second measured quantity in, which is what a 'product' step is for

label.description: What this number IS, e.g. 'Steigung', 'Bruttogeschossfläche', 'Grundfläche'. Empty ONLY for a bare constant that names itself, such as the 100 of a percentage — everything a reader has to look up needs its name under it

provenance.description: Where `value` came from, copied from the ifc_measure answer's own provenance: 'declared' (the IFC file states it), 'computed' (we measured it off the geometry), 'inferred' (a heuristic). Leave null for a figure the user typed or a limit read out of the Bestimmung. NEVER guess it

source.description: Optional half-line naming WHERE the figure is written down, e.g. 'Einreichplan, Schnitt A-A' or 'Bebauungsplan PD 8123'. Revealed when the reader expands the derivation's sources

step.description: Instead of a value: the 1-based index of an EARLIER step whose result this operand is. Must point strictly backwards. With this set, leave value, unit, provenance and tolerance null — the renderer takes them from the step it names

schema.description:
Emit for the arithmetic behind a number — the Rechenweg a Ziviltechniker re-checks.

Whenever the answer computes something (a GFZ, a Brandabschnitt's
Netto-Grundfläche, a Brandlast, a required parking count), this card is the
derivation laid out line by line instead of a sentence the reader has to
re-derive to trust. The four named rules are NOT a calculation: a U-value
from its layers, the Schrittmaßregel, an escape route's Gehweglänge and a
Lichteintrittsfläche are a `formula`, which owns their bounds.

YOU SUPPLY THE INPUTS, NEVER THE ANSWER. Give each operand its label, value
and unit, name the operation, and give the limit if there is one. The card
evaluates every step itself, carries the tolerance bands through, formats
the numbers in Austrian convention and decides pass/fail. There is no field
for a result, and that absence is the feature: a stated result that
disagreed with its own operands would be the worst artefact this product can
produce, because this is the part that gets screenshotted into a submission.

Several steps chain by reference: a later operand can name an earlier step
(`step: 1`) instead of carrying a value, so a two-stage derivation stays
auditable rather than collapsing into one pre-computed figure.

reference.description: Where the RULE behind the derivation is written (the limit may carry its own)

steps.description: The derivation in order, most cards one step. A later step may reference an earlier one's result

card:daylight_incidence.description:
Building blocks (reused object shapes):
  DimensionCheck = { label*: string (What is measured, e.g. 'lichte Durchgangsbreite'; non-empty), value: number (Actual measurement (drawn); null if unknown), required: number (OIB limit for this dimension), unit: string (Unit for both value and required, e.g. 'cm', 'm', '%'; default "cm"), comparator: "<=" | ">=" (How actual must relate to required), status*: "pass" | "fail" | "warning" | "needs_input" (Verdict for this dimension), provenance: "declared" | "computed" | "inferred" (Where `value` came from, copied from the ifc_measure answer's own provenance: 'declared' (the IFC file states it), 'computed' (we measured it off the geometry), 'inferred' (a heuristic, offered for confirmation). Leave null when the number did not come from the model at all — a figure the user typed, or one taken from the Bestimmung. NEVER guess it: labelling our own measurement 'declared' turns our tolerance into the architect's claim.), tolerance: number (The ± band on `value`, in the SAME unit — copied from the ifc_measure answer. Only meaningful with provenance 'computed': a declared figure is the file's statement and has no band of ours. A measured dimension without its band reads as exact, and the band is what decides whether 2.49 m clears a 2.50 m minimum.; >= 0), missing: string (With status 'needs_input': what the export does not provide and WHAT TO CHANGE IN THE CAD to make it answerable — copied verbatim from the ifc_measure answer's missing.remedy. This is the sentence the architect acts on, and a card that shows an empty slot instead of it turns a finding about the export into a blank the reader reads as a fact about the building.) }
  Obstruction = { distance_m*: number (Horizontal distance from the window in metres; > 0), height_m*: number (Height of the obstruction above the window sill in metres), label*: string (What it is, e.g. 'Gegenüberliegendes Gebäude'; non-empty) }
  NormReference = { document*: string (Regulation name, e.g. 'OIB-Richtlinie 2', 'ÖNORM B 1600'; non-empty), section: string (Clause/table, e.g. 'Pkt. 5.1.1', 'Tabelle 1b'), edition: string (Edition/year, e.g. 'Ausgabe Mai 2023'), excerpt: string (Literal quoted sentence grounding the value (<= ~200 chars)) }

Card types:
  - "daylight_incidence"
      shape: { title*: string (non-empty), room_floor_area_m2: number, glass_area*: DimensionCheck, window_sill_height_m: number, window_head_height_m: number, obstruction: Obstruction, reference*: NormReference, note: string }

Numbers that came from a MEASUREMENT (`ifc_measure`):
  Every ifc_measure answer says HOW it was obtained. When you put one of its numbers on a
  card, carry that with it — on DimensionCheck, set `provenance` to the answer's own
  provenance, and for a 'computed' one set `tolerance` to the ± band in the SAME unit.
  Copy them; never infer them. Marking our own measurement 'declared' turns our tolerance
  into the architect's claim, and a measured dimension shown without its band reads as
  exact — which is what decides whether 2.47 m clears a 2.50 m minimum.
  Leave both null for a number that did not come from the model: a figure the user typed,
  or a limit read out of the Bestimmung. Null means 'not stated', never 'declared'.
  When the answer came back `decidable: false`, the dimension is status 'needs_input' with
  `value` null and `missing` set to that answer's missing.remedy, VERBATIM — that sentence
  is what the architect changes in their CAD. A blank slot instead of it reads as a fact
  about the building, when it is a finding about the export.

Every text field is PLAIN TEXT:
  No card renders markdown. Write the words, not the markup — no [text](url) links, no
  **bold**, no `code`. A card that needs a link to its source already has one: the card
  builds it from the fields you filled in, so writing one yourself adds a second, unchecked
  claim next to the checked one.

Worked examples (copy the nesting exactly):
  daylight_incidence:
    {"type": "daylight_incidence", "title": "Belichtung – freier Lichteinfall (Gästezimmer)", "room_floor_area_m2": 25, "glass_area": {"label": "Lichteintrittsfläche", "value": 3.0, "required": 2.5, "unit": "m²", "comparator": ">=", "status": "pass"}, "window_sill_height_m": 0.9, "window_head_height_m": 2.4, "reference": {"document": "OIB-Richtlinie 3", "section": "Pkt. 9.1.1", "edition": "Ausgabe Mai 2023"}}

schema.description:
A document the agent wrote into this conversation's working directory.

System-emitted by the working directory's ``write_file`` / ``edit_file``, and
again by ``file_draft`` once the draft has become a project document.

**The card has two states, and the difference is three fields.** Unfiled, it
reports a file that exists in this conversation and nowhere else: not filed,
not indexed, not citable, not in the Files pane. Filed, it names a
``documents`` row — and then it can offer the two things a reader wants,
opening it and sending it for review, both through the routes the Files pane
itself uses.

The three fields travel together or not at all: a card carrying a
``document_id`` and no ``version_state`` could not say whether the draft is
still submittable, and one carrying a state with no ``version_id`` could not
submit it. ``_require_filed_together`` is what refuses the half-filled shape,
because the alternative is a card that renders a live-looking control over
nothing.

card:egress_diagram.description:
Building blocks (reused object shapes):
  EgressSegment = { label*: string (Segment label, e.g. 'Raum → Gang', 'Gang → Treppenhaus'; non-empty), length_m*: number (Run length in metres (drawn to scale); > 0), turn: "straight" | "left" | "right" (Turn AFTER this run; default "straight") }
  DimensionCheck = { label*: string (What is measured, e.g. 'lichte Durchgangsbreite'; non-empty), value: number (Actual measurement (drawn); null if unknown), required: number (OIB limit for this dimension), unit: string (Unit for both value and required, e.g. 'cm', 'm', '%'; default "cm"), comparator: "<=" | ">=" (How actual must relate to required), status*: "pass" | "fail" | "warning" | "needs_input" (Verdict for this dimension), provenance: "declared" | "computed" | "inferred" (Where `value` came from, copied from the ifc_measure answer's own provenance: 'declared' (the IFC file states it), 'computed' (we measured it off the geometry), 'inferred' (a heuristic, offered for confirmation). Leave null when the number did not come from the model at all — a figure the user typed, or one taken from the Bestimmung. NEVER guess it: labelling our own measurement 'declared' turns our tolerance into the architect's claim.), tolerance: number (The ± band on `value`, in the SAME unit — copied from the ifc_measure answer. Only meaningful with provenance 'computed': a declared figure is the file's statement and has no band of ours. A measured dimension without its band reads as exact, and the band is what decides whether 2.49 m clears a 2.50 m minimum.; >= 0), missing: string (With status 'needs_input': what the export does not provide and WHAT TO CHANGE IN THE CAD to make it answerable — copied verbatim from the ifc_measure answer's missing.remedy. This is the sentence the architect acts on, and a card that shows an empty slot instead of it turns a finding about the export into a blank the reader reads as a fact about the building.) }
  NormReference = { document*: string (Regulation name, e.g. 'OIB-Richtlinie 2', 'ÖNORM B 1600'; non-empty), section: string (Clause/table, e.g. 'Pkt. 5.1.1', 'Tabelle 1b'), edition: string (Edition/year, e.g. 'Ausgabe Mai 2023'), excerpt: string (Literal quoted sentence grounding the value (<= ~200 chars)) }

Card types:
  - "egress_diagram"
      shape: { title*: string (non-empty), segments*: [EgressSegment], total_length*: DimensionCheck, start_label: string (default "ungünstigster Punkt"), exit_label: string (default "Treppenhaus"), reference*: NormReference }

Numbers that came from a MEASUREMENT (`ifc_measure`):
  Every ifc_measure answer says HOW it was obtained. When you put one of its numbers on a
  card, carry that with it — on DimensionCheck, set `provenance` to the answer's own
  provenance, and for a 'computed' one set `tolerance` to the ± band in the SAME unit.
  Copy them; never infer them. Marking our own measurement 'declared' turns our tolerance
  into the architect's claim, and a measured dimension shown without its band reads as
  exact — which is what decides whether 2.47 m clears a 2.50 m minimum.
  Leave both null for a number that did not come from the model: a figure the user typed,
  or a limit read out of the Bestimmung. Null means 'not stated', never 'declared'.
  When the answer came back `decidable: false`, the dimension is status 'needs_input' with
  `value` null and `missing` set to that answer's missing.remedy, VERBATIM — that sentence
  is what the architect changes in their CAD. A blank slot instead of it reads as a fact
  about the building, when it is a finding about the export.

Every text field is PLAIN TEXT:
  No card renders markdown. Write the words, not the markup — no [text](url) links, no
  **bold**, no `code`. A card that needs a link to its source already has one: the card
  builds it from the fields you filled in, so writing one yourself adds a second, unchecked
  claim next to the checked one.

DimensionCheck.description:
One measured dimension drawn on a schematic and checked against a limit.

`value` is the project's actual measurement (drawn to scale); `required` is
the OIB limit. If `value` is unknown, leave it null and set status
'needs_input'.

## Why a number here carries where it came from

This block used to be `label / value / required / unit / comparator /
status` and nothing else, and that made the card the least honest surface in
the product. `ifc_measure` answers „gemessen: 2.47 m (±5 mm) — aus der
Geometrie berechnet, nicht deklariert“, the assistant repeats that in the
prose, and the card beside it drew **2.47 m ✓** — indistinguishable from a
figure the architect had stated in their own file. The card is the part a
reviewer screenshots into a submission, so the surface that dropped the
qualifier was the surface most likely to be forwarded without it.

Three fields close that, and all three are OPTIONAL: a card built from the
Bestimmung alone (a limit with no model behind it) has nothing to put in
them, and a null here means "not stated", never "declared".

comparator.title: Comparator

missing.description: With status 'needs_input': what the export does not provide and WHAT TO CHANGE IN THE CAD to make it answerable — copied verbatim from the ifc_measure answer's missing.remedy. This is the sentence the architect acts on, and a card that shows an empty slot instead of it turns a finding about the export into a blank the reader reads as a fact about the building.
missing.title: Missing

provenance.description: Where `value` came from, copied from the ifc_measure answer's own provenance: 'declared' (the IFC file states it), 'computed' (we measured it off the geometry), 'inferred' (a heuristic, offered for confirmation). Leave null when the number did not come from the model at all — a figure the user typed, or one taken from the Bestimmung. NEVER guess it: labelling our own measurement 'declared' turns our tolerance into the architect's claim.
provenance.title: Provenance

tolerance.description: The ± band on `value`, in the SAME unit — copied from the ifc_measure answer. Only meaningful with provenance 'computed': a declared figure is the file's statement and has no band of ours. A measured dimension without its band reads as exact, and the band is what decides whether 2.49 m clears a 2.50 m minimum.
tolerance.title: Tolerance

unit.description: Unit for both value and required, e.g. 'cm', 'm', '%'

FileOperationItem.description:
One proposed change, in the vocabulary of the operation that owns it.

Deliberately flat with per-operation fields rather than a nested union: the
card is built by the tool, validated once here, and rendered by one
component that switches on the CARD's `operation` — a shape the frontend's
generated Zod can narrow without a second discriminator inside every row.
:meth:`FileOperationProposalCard._require_operation_fields` is what keeps a
row from carrying another operation's fields.

``document`` is a FILE NAME and never an id. The agent's inventory
(``knowledge/inventory.py``) knows files by ``(collection, file_name)`` and
has no document ids in it at all, so a card carrying an id would be
carrying something the tool invented. The reader's session resolves the
name against their own document list when they accept.

current.description: What this is TODAY (current folder or name) — for the before/after line
current.title: Current

document.description: File name exactly as the inventory lists it (move, rename, assign)
document.title: Document

folder_name.description: create_folder: the new folder's own name (one segment)
folder_name.title: Folder Name

member.description: assign: the person as the user named them; the reader's session resolves it against the project
member.title: Member

parent_folder.description: create_folder: the parent folder PATH, or an empty string for the project root
parent_folder.title: Parent Folder

reason.description: Why this change, one short sentence the reader sees under the row
reason.title: Reason

source.description: Which shelf the document sits on, so the name resolves in the right corpus
source.title: Source

target_folder.description: move: the destination folder PATH, e.g. 'Einreichung/Akten'. Empty string is the project root
target_folder.title: Target Folder

schema.description:
A workspace change the agent PROPOSES and a person applies.

System-emitted by ``propose_file_change`` (``packages/agent/src/agent/tools/files/``).
Every operation is a write, none of them writes: the tool's own result text
says plainly that nothing has changed yet. With ``proposal_id`` the card
shows a proposal stored on the server (ADR-0105), which the server applies
in the accepting person's session; it then carries the one operation of
the call that created it. Without one (an older BFF, a run with no
envelope, a refusal) the proposal was not stored: the UI draws the card
read-only, saying so, and the browser executes nothing.

note.description: One line of context under the list, when it adds something
note.title: Note

operation.description: Which verb every entry in `operations` is
operation.title: Operation

operations.description: The proposed changes, in the order they will be applied
operations.title: Operations

proposal_id.description: The server proposal this card shows (POST /api/internal/proposals). Absent: the proposal was not stored, and the card is a read-only notice that nothing was proposed
proposal_id.title: Proposal Id

title.description: Short action title, e.g. 'Vier Dateien in „Einreichung“ verschieben'
title.title: Title

DaylightRatioFormula.description:
Lichteintrittsfläche against the room's Bodenfläche (OIB-RL 3 Pkt. 9.1.1, 9.1.3, 9.1.4).

The required share is 12 %, raised to 15 % by an overhang over 1,50 m, by
2 % per started metre of overhang beyond 3,00 m, and by 1 % per started
metre of room depth beyond 5,00 m; the renderer derives it from the inputs.
The free light angle of 45° (Pkt. 9.1.2) is a precondition the card states
and does not check.

UValueFormula.description:
U = 1 / (R_si + Σ d/λ + R_se), for an opaque component of homogeneous layers (ÖNORM EN ISO 6946).

`component` picks the row of OIB-RL 6 Pkt. 4.4.1 the card holds the U-value
against, and with it the heat-flow direction for the surface resistances:
an external wall (row 1, horizontal), a ceiling or roof slope against
outside air (row 18, upward; a slope steeper than 60° counts as a wall),
a ceiling over outside air such as a passage (row 22, downward). Only
components against outside air: elsewhere R_se is not the standard's 0,04.
Air layers, inhomogeneous layers and the standard's corrections are out of
scope.

`measure` picks the requirement: a new build (Pkt. 4.4.1, the table), or a
renovation by single measures or the renewal of a component (Pkt. 4.5),
which without a Sanierungskonzept is the table value less 24 %. A major
renovation (größere Renovierung) is held to the energy figures of Pkt. 4.3,
not to a component's U-value, so the card computes U and does not judge it.
Unknown: the card cannot judge, because the bound depends on it.

component.description: Which component: 'external_wall', 'roof_or_ceiling_to_outside_air' (a ceiling or roof slope, slopes over 60° are walls), 'floor_over_outside_air' (a ceiling over a passage or parking deck)
component.title: Component

measure.description: 'new_build' (Pkt. 4.4.1), 'renovation' (single measures or a renewed component, Pkt. 4.5) or 'major_renovation' (a größere Renovierung, held to the energy figures of Pkt. 4.3, which this card does not judge). Read it from the project context (existing_or_new); null when it is not known, and the card then says it cannot judge
measure.title: Measure

schema.description:
Emit for a number worked out by one of four named rules, so the reader can ask "what if" on the card.

The rules: a U-value from its layers (u_value), the Schrittmaßregel and the
stair table (stair_step_rule), an escape route's Gehweglänge
(escape_route_length), the Lichteintrittsfläche against the Bodenfläche
(daylight_ratio). Anything else worked out is a `calculation`.

YOU SUPPLY THE CASE AND THE INPUTS, NEVER A NUMBER OF YOUR OWN. Name the
case the rule asks for (`stair_type`, `component`, `start`) and fill each
input from the project's documents, the user's own figures or the norm,
with `source` saying where it is written. An input you do not have stays
null: the card says it cannot judge, and the reader can enter an
assumption. The card computes, takes the bound from the Richtlinie's table
for that case, judges, and recomputes when the reader changes an input.
The title names the component („U-Wert Außenwand AW 01"), never a value.

card:guardrail_check.description:
Building blocks (reused object shapes):
  DimensionCheck = { label*: string (What is measured, e.g. 'lichte Durchgangsbreite'; non-empty), value: number (Actual measurement (drawn); null if unknown), required: number (OIB limit for this dimension), unit: string (Unit for both value and required, e.g. 'cm', 'm', '%'; default "cm"), comparator: "<=" | ">=" (How actual must relate to required), status*: "pass" | "fail" | "warning" | "needs_input" (Verdict for this dimension), provenance: "declared" | "computed" | "inferred" (Where `value` came from, copied from the ifc_measure answer's own provenance: 'declared' (the IFC file states it), 'computed' (we measured it off the geometry), 'inferred' (a heuristic, offered for confirmation). Leave null when the number did not come from the model at all — a figure the user typed, or one taken from the Bestimmung. NEVER guess it: labelling our own measurement 'declared' turns our tolerance into the architect's claim.), tolerance: number (The ± band on `value`, in the SAME unit — copied from the ifc_measure answer. Only meaningful with provenance 'computed': a declared figure is the file's statement and has no band of ours. A measured dimension without its band reads as exact, and the band is what decides whether 2.49 m clears a 2.50 m minimum.; >= 0), missing: string (With status 'needs_input': what the export does not provide and WHAT TO CHANGE IN THE CAD to make it answerable — copied verbatim from the ifc_measure answer's missing.remedy. This is the sentence the architect acts on, and a card that shows an empty slot instead of it turns a finding about the export into a blank the reader reads as a fact about the building.) }
  NormReference = { document*: string (Regulation name, e.g. 'OIB-Richtlinie 2', 'ÖNORM B 1600'; non-empty), section: string (Clause/table, e.g. 'Pkt. 5.1.1', 'Tabelle 1b'), edition: string (Edition/year, e.g. 'Ausgabe Mai 2023'), excerpt: string (Literal quoted sentence grounding the value (<= ~200 chars)) }

Card types:
  - "guardrail_check"
      shape: { title*: string (non-empty), context*: "balcony" | "loggia" | "staircase" | "window" | "roof_terrace", fall_height*: DimensionCheck, rail_height*: DimensionCheck, max_opening*: DimensionCheck, bottom_gap: DimensionCheck, has_horizontal_elements_in_climb_zone: boolean, reference*: NormReference, note: string }

Numbers that came from a MEASUREMENT (`ifc_measure`):
  Every ifc_measure answer says HOW it was obtained. When you put one of its numbers on a
  card, carry that with it — on DimensionCheck, set `provenance` to the answer's own
  provenance, and for a 'computed' one set `tolerance` to the ± band in the SAME unit.
  Copy them; never infer them. Marking our own measurement 'declared' turns our tolerance
  into the architect's claim, and a measured dimension shown without its band reads as
  exact — which is what decides whether 2.47 m clears a 2.50 m minimum.
  Leave both null for a number that did not come from the model: a figure the user typed,
  or a limit read out of the Bestimmung. Null means 'not stated', never 'declared'.
  When the answer came back `decidable: false`, the dimension is status 'needs_input' with
  `value` null and `missing` set to that answer's missing.remedy, VERBATIM — that sentence
  is what the architect changes in their CAD. A blank slot instead of it reads as a fact
  about the building, when it is a finding about the export.

Every text field is PLAIN TEXT:
  No card renders markdown. Write the words, not the markup — no [text](url) links, no
  **bold**, no `code`. A card that needs a link to its source already has one: the card
  builds it from the fields you filled in, so writing one yourself adds a second, unchecked
  claim next to the checked one.

DimensionCheck.description:
One measured dimension drawn on a schematic and checked against a limit.

`value` is the project's actual measurement (drawn to scale); `required` is
the OIB limit. If `value` is unknown, leave it null and set status
'needs_input'.

## Why a number here carries where it came from

This block used to be `label / value / required / unit / comparator /
status` and nothing else, and that made the card the least honest surface in
the product. `ifc_measure` answers „gemessen: 2.47 m (±5 mm) — aus der
Geometrie berechnet, nicht deklariert“, the assistant repeats that in the
prose, and the card beside it drew **2.47 m ✓** — indistinguishable from a
figure the architect had stated in their own file. The card is the part a
reviewer screenshots into a submission, so the surface that dropped the
qualifier was the surface most likely to be forwarded without it.

Three fields close that, and all three are OPTIONAL: a card built from the
Bestimmung alone (a limit with no model behind it) has nothing to put in
them, and a null here means "not stated", never "declared".

comparator.description: How actual must relate to required
comparator.title: Comparator

missing.description: With status 'needs_input': what the export does not provide and WHAT TO CHANGE IN THE CAD to make it answerable — copied verbatim from the ifc_measure answer's missing.remedy. This is the sentence the architect acts on, and a card that shows an empty slot instead of it turns a finding about the export into a blank the reader reads as a fact about the building.
missing.title: Missing

provenance.description: Where `value` came from, copied from the ifc_measure answer's own provenance: 'declared' (the IFC file states it), 'computed' (we measured it off the geometry), 'inferred' (a heuristic, offered for confirmation). Leave null when the number did not come from the model at all — a figure the user typed, or one taken from the Bestimmung. NEVER guess it: labelling our own measurement 'declared' turns our tolerance into the architect's claim.
provenance.title: Provenance

tolerance.description: The ± band on `value`, in the SAME unit — copied from the ifc_measure answer. Only meaningful with provenance 'computed': a declared figure is the file's statement and has no band of ours. A measured dimension without its band reads as exact, and the band is what decides whether 2.49 m clears a 2.50 m minimum.
tolerance.title: Tolerance

unit.description: Unit for both value and required, e.g. 'cm', 'm', '%'
unit.title: Unit

DimensionCheck.title: DimensionCheck

NormReference.description:
A verifiable pointer into a regulation (the atom of grounding).

Every required value MUST carry one so the architect can verify it against
the source. Never fabricate a reference.

excerpt.description: Literal quoted sentence grounding the value (<= ~200 chars)
excerpt.title: Excerpt

NormReference.title: NormReference

The Prüfbuch: OIB requirements with their verdict against this model.

Carries only WHICH requirements to show; the frontend runs the catalogue and
renders the counts, the thresholds and the failing elements itself. The
model therefore cannot state that a building complies, because it never
supplies a verdict — the same reason the schedule card carries no areas.

Use when the user asks whether the model meets a requirement, what is still
open, or what they have to add to the model. Prefer it over prose whenever
the answer is a list of requirements: the card stays correct after the model
changes, and a sentence does not.

NEVER present this as proof of compliance (a Nachweis). The catalogue reads only published
property values, it reads no geometry, and escape-route lengths, guardrail
heights and fire-compartment sizes are not in it at all.

IfcElementMatch.description:
The SET of elements to highlight, as a filter rather than a list of ids.

Exactly the ``filters`` object passed to ``ifc_query`` — the browser re-runs
it against the model, so the highlight covers every matching element and
nothing has to survive the model's context window.

``ifc_query`` spells its filter keys in camelCase (``ifcTypes``,
``nameContains``) and this card is authored in snake_case like every other
card field. The agent is told to reuse the filter it already wrote, so BOTH
spellings are accepted and normalise to the snake_case field: without the
aliases a copied filter validated cleanly with every key silently dropped,
leaving an empty match, and a highlight group that selects nothing.

IfcHighlight.description:
One set of model elements to call out, with a verdict.

EXACTLY ONE of ``match`` or ``global_ids`` — never both, never neither.
(Stated here because the rendered card catalogue lists a model's fields
from ``model_fields`` and never sees a ``model_validator``: both selectors
therefore appear as plain optionals, and the worked example — one group of
each kind — reads as permission to supply both. A highlight that does is
dropped, taking its whole card with it.)

Prefer ``match`` whenever the
answer is about a set rather than about elements you named. An id list has
to travel through the model's context, so "the 420 external walls" arrived
as whatever fitted and the card highlighted a fraction of the answer while
the legend claimed all of it. A filter is re-run in the browser: the whole
set lights up, and it costs the model a filter it has already written.

Use for a handful of elements the answer names; use 'match' for a set. When the answer came from a MEASUREMENT, the ids to highlight are the ones the measurement itself names: every ifc_measure answer ends with a 'Bezug:' line listing exactly the elements the number was derived from, and highlighting those shows the user the thing that was measured rather than a description of it.

card:setback_plan.description:
Building blocks (reused object shapes):
  SetbackSide = { side*: "front" | "back" | "left" | "right" (Which edge), required_m*: number (Required setback in metres (OIB/Bauordnung)), actual_m: number (Actual distance in metres; null if unknown), status*: "pass" | "fail" | "warning" | "needs_input" (Verdict for this side) }
  DimensionCheck = { label*: string (What is measured, e.g. 'lichte Durchgangsbreite'; non-empty), value: number (Actual measurement (drawn); null if unknown), required: number (OIB limit for this dimension), unit: string (Unit for both value and required, e.g. 'cm', 'm', '%'; default "cm"), comparator: "<=" | ">=" (How actual must relate to required), status*: "pass" | "fail" | "warning" | "needs_input" (Verdict for this dimension), provenance: "declared" | "computed" | "inferred" (Where `value` came from, copied from the ifc_measure answer's own provenance: 'declared' (the IFC file states it), 'computed' (we measured it off the geometry), 'inferred' (a heuristic, offered for confirmation). Leave null when the number did not come from the model at all — a figure the user typed, or one taken from the Bestimmung. NEVER guess it: labelling our own measurement 'declared' turns our tolerance into the architect's claim.), tolerance: number (The ± band on `value`, in the SAME unit — copied from the ifc_measure answer. Only meaningful with provenance 'computed': a declared figure is the file's statement and has no band of ours. A measured dimension without its band reads as exact, and the band is what decides whether 2.49 m clears a 2.50 m minimum.; >= 0), missing: string (With status 'needs_input': what the export does not provide and WHAT TO CHANGE IN THE CAD to make it answerable — copied verbatim from the ifc_measure answer's missing.remedy. This is the sentence the architect acts on, and a card that shows an empty slot instead of it turns a finding about the export into a blank the reader reads as a fact about the building.) }
  NormReference = { document*: string (Regulation name, e.g. 'OIB-Richtlinie 2', 'ÖNORM B 1600'; non-empty), section: string (Clause/table, e.g. 'Pkt. 5.1.1', 'Tabelle 1b'), edition: string (Edition/year, e.g. 'Ausgabe Mai 2023'), excerpt: string (Literal quoted sentence grounding the value (<= ~200 chars)) }

Card types:
  - "setback_plan"
      shape: { title*: string (non-empty), parcel_width_m: number (> 0), parcel_depth_m: number (> 0), building_width_m: number (> 0), building_depth_m: number (> 0), sides*: [SetbackSide], parcel_area_m2: number (> 0), footprint_area_m2: number (> 0), gross_floor_area_m2: number (> 0), coverage: DimensionCheck, density: DimensionCheck, reference*: NormReference }

Numbers that came from a MEASUREMENT (`ifc_measure`):
  Every ifc_measure answer says HOW it was obtained. When you put one of its numbers on a
  card, carry that with it — on DimensionCheck, set `provenance` to the answer's own
  provenance, and for a 'computed' one set `tolerance` to the ± band in the SAME unit.
  Copy them; never infer them. Marking our own measurement 'declared' turns our tolerance
  into the architect's claim, and a measured dimension shown without its band reads as
  exact — which is what decides whether 2.47 m clears a 2.50 m minimum.
  Leave both null for a number that did not come from the model: a figure the user typed,
  or a limit read out of the Bestimmung. Null means 'not stated', never 'declared'.
  When the answer came back `decidable: false`, the dimension is status 'needs_input' with
  `value` null and `missing` set to that answer's missing.remedy, VERBATIM — that sentence
  is what the architect changes in their CAD. A blank slot instead of it reads as a fact
  about the building, when it is a finding about the export.

Every text field is PLAIN TEXT:
  No card renders markdown. Write the words, not the markup — no [text](url) links, no
  **bold**, no `code`. A card that needs a link to its source already has one: the card
  builds it from the fields you filled in, so writing one yourself adds a second, unchecked
  claim next to the checked one.

DimensionCheck.description:
One measured dimension drawn on a schematic and checked against a limit.

`value` is the project's actual measurement (drawn to scale); `required` is
the OIB limit. If `value` is unknown, leave it null and set status
'needs_input'.

## Why a number here carries where it came from

This block used to be `label / value / required / unit / comparator /
status` and nothing else, and that made the card the least honest surface in
the product. `ifc_measure` answers „gemessen: 2.47 m (±5 mm) — aus der
Geometrie berechnet, nicht deklariert“, the assistant repeats that in the
prose, and the card beside it drew **2.47 m ✓** — indistinguishable from a
figure the architect had stated in their own file. The card is the part a
reviewer screenshots into a submission, so the surface that dropped the
qualifier was the surface most likely to be forwarded without it.

Three fields close that, and all three are OPTIONAL: a card built from the
Bestimmung alone (a limit with no model behind it) has nothing to put in
them, and a null here means "not stated", never "declared".

comparator.title: Comparator

missing.description: With status 'needs_input': what the export does not provide and WHAT TO CHANGE IN THE CAD to make it answerable — copied verbatim from the ifc_measure answer's missing.remedy. This is the sentence the architect acts on, and a card that shows an empty slot instead of it turns a finding about the export into a blank the reader reads as a fact about the building.
missing.title: Missing

Leave null when the number did not come from the model at all — a figure the user typed, or one taken from the Bestimmung. NEVER guess it: labelling our own measurement 'declared' turns our tolerance into the architect's claim.
provenance.title: Provenance

tolerance.description: The ± band on `value`, in the SAME unit — copied from the ifc_measure answer. Only meaningful with provenance 'computed': a declared figure is the file's statement and has no band of ours. A measured dimension without its band reads as exact, and the band is what decides whether 2.49 m clears a 2.50 m minimum.

card:surface.description:
COMPOSE. Variants the reader picks ONE of to read (two designs, two Bundesländer, Bestand against Umbau, Außentreppe against zweites Treppenhaus) travel as ONE `surface` card, an A2UI v0.9 component list with a `Tabs` root, one tab per variant. A tab holds a card, or a `Text` holding the Markdown you would otherwise write for that variant: its table, its Status column, its steps, its [N]. What holds for every variant stays in the prose above the tabs, and the prose names the difference that decides between them; the tabs carry the detail. `Row` (side by side where the screen is wide) and `Column` (in order) put cards that read together into one slot. The container has id "root"; every other component is a card named by its type with that card's own fields, or `{"id", "component": "Text", "text": "<Markdown>"}`; children are referenced by id, each in ONE place (no id listed twice, no leaf in two tabs). Limits: a `Row` or `Column` holds 2 to 4 children, `Tabs` 2 to 6 tabs, the surface 2 to 6 leaves; a `Text` is at most 4000 characters and carries no card or callout marker (those are placed from the prose). Never an interactive or tool card inside, nor an envelope field (verdict, summary, takeaways, callout), and a surface counts as one card against the ceiling. Two tabs that say nearly the same are one answer, not variants.
{"type": "surface", "title": "Zweiter Fluchtweg — zwei Varianten", "components": [{"id": "root", "component": "Tabs", "tabs": [{"title": "Außentreppe", "child": "a"}, {"title": "Zweites Treppenhaus", "child": "b"}]}, {"id": "a", "component": "Text", "text": "| Kriterium | Anforderung | Status | Fundstelle |
|---|---|---|---|
…"}, {"id": "b", "component": "Text", "text": "1. …
2. …"}]}

schema.description:
Several cards composed into one A2UI surface: variants as tabs, related cards side by side.

`components` is an A2UI v0.9 component list (a2ui.org): flat, each entry
`{"id", "component", …props}`, children referenced by id, exactly one
`"id": "root"`. Containers are `Row` and `Column` (`children`: ids) and
`Tabs` (`tabs`: `[{title, child}]`); `Text` (`text`: Markdown) holds what
the answer would write in prose, a table or a list; every other component
is a card, named by its type, with that card's own fields as props. Validated twice: the
structure by `a2ui-core` (unique ids, a root, no dangling reference, no
cycle, no orphan), each card by its own model.

components.description: The A2UI component list: one container with id 'root' (Row, Column or Tabs) and what it holds: cards, each `{"id", "component": <card type>, …that card's fields}`, and `{"id", "component": "Text", "text": <Markdown>}` for a table, a list or prose.
components.title: Components

title.description: Optional heading over the whole surface, e.g. 'Zwei Varianten des zweiten Fluchtwegs'
title.title: Title

schema.description:
Work the agent has taken on, as a row somebody can come back to.

System-emitted by ``create_task``. What it exists to prevent is the answer
„ich mache den Einreichcheck bis Freitag“ with nothing behind it: the card is
proof there is a row, and the row is what carries the requester's permission,
the deadline and — when a person judges the result — the decision that reaches
the next attempt (ADR-0051).

Informational, not interactive. The task is already queued when this renders,
so there is no Accept: a control would either repeat the delegation or cancel
it, and cancelling delegated work is a Files-and-tasks surface decision, not
a chat one.

``conversation_id`` is the thread the run writes into, so the card can link a
reader to the work rather than only announce it. Absent when the run's
conversation could not be created, which is the same degraded shape a
scheduled job has had since jobs got conversations at all.

conversation_id.description: The conversation the run writes into; absent when it could not be created
conversation_id.title: Conversation Id

due_at.description: ISO instant the work is wanted by, or absent when none was named
due_at.title: Due At

goal.description: What was asked, in the requester's own words
goal.title: Goal

kind.description: What kind of work was delegated
kind.title: Kind

title.description: What the task is called in the inbox and the list
title.title: Title

CalculationOperand.description: What this number IS, e.g. 'Steigung', 'Bruttogeschossfläche', 'Grundfläche'. Empty ONLY for a bare constant that names itself, such as the 100 of a percentage — everything a reader has to look up needs its name under it
CalculationOperand.name: label

CalculationOperand.description: The number itself. Leave null when it is not known — the renderer then shows the step as undecidable instead of a result, which is the honest outcome. Must be null when `step` is set
CalculationOperand.name: value

CalculationOperand.description: Unit of this operand, e.g. 'cm', 'm²', 'MJ'; omit for a bare count or a ratio
CalculationOperand.name: unit

CalculationOperand.description: Only on a 'sum': the RULE's own multiplier for this term, e.g. 2 for a two-sided Abstand. Negative subtracts the term. Omit for a plain +1 — never use it to smuggle a second measured quantity in, which is what a 'product' step is for
CalculationOperand.name: factor

CalculationOperand.description: Instead of a value: the 1-based index of an EARLIER step whose result this operand is. Must point strictly backwards. With this set, leave value, unit, provenance and tolerance null — the renderer takes them from the step it names
CalculationOperand.name: step

CalculationOperand.description: Where `value` came from, copied from the ifc_measure answer's own provenance: 'declared' (the IFC file states it), 'computed' (we measured it off the geometry), 'inferred' (a heuristic). Leave null for a figure the user typed or a limit read out of the Bestimmung. NEVER guess it
CalculationOperand.name: provenance

CalculationOperand.description: The ± band on `value`, in the SAME unit — copied from the ifc_measure answer, and only meaningful with provenance 'computed'. The renderer propagates it through every following step, so this is what decides whether the derived result is genuinely on one side of a limit
CalculationOperand.name: tolerance

CalculationOperand.description: Optional half-line naming WHERE the figure is written down, e.g. 'Einreichplan, Schnitt A-A' or 'Bebauungsplan PD 8123'. Revealed when the reader expands the derivation's sources
CalculationOperand.name: source

CalculationStep.description: Which of the five shapes this step is: 'sum' (Σ factor × value), 'product' (Π value), 'quotient' (first ÷ second), 'percent_of' (second, as a percentage, OF first), 'percent_ratio' (first ÷ second × 100, a percentage)
CalculationStep.name: operation

CalculationStep.description: The numbers going in, in the order they are read. 'quotient', 'percent_of' and 'percent_ratio' take EXACTLY two
CalculationStep.name: operands

CalculationStep.description: Unit of THIS step's result, e.g. 'cm', 'm²', 'W/(m²K)'; omit for a dimensionless ratio like a GFZ. Ignored on 'percent_ratio', whose result is always a percentage

tool:chat.files.estate+drafts+skills:glo.description: Finds files by name. `pattern` takes `*`, `**`, `?`, `[abc]` and `{a,b}` (`**/*Brandschutz*`); case is ignored and ä/ae, ö/oe, ü/ue, ß/ss are folded, so `*Flaeche*` finds `Flächenwidmung`. `path` limits it to one folder; without it every mount is searched. Returns absolute paths, each with pages and Dokumentart, at most 100. Names only: for words inside documents use grep, for a topic knowledge_search.

tool:chat.files.estate+drafts+skills:gre.description:
Finds wording inside documents: which files and pages contain a word, a number, a name, a Geschäftszahl or a clause reference, and shows that it stands nowhere else. Literal by default: case, ä/ae, ö/oe, ü/ue, ß/ss, soft hyphens and words split at a line break are folded, and a pattern of two or three characters matches whole words only. `mode="regex"` takes a regular expression (Python syntax, case-insensitive, `MA 37/\d{6}`). `stemmed=true` also matches inflected German forms. `path` limits the search to a folder or one document and `glob` filters file names; without `path` every document mount is searched, the OIB corpus included, and the drafts only with a /drafts/ path.
`output_mode`: `files_with_matches` (default) gives each matching file with its count and pages and how many files were searched; `content` gives the matching pages as citable passages (up to 8, spread over files) and the lines around each match (`context`, 0 to 3, adds lines); `count` gives occurrences per file. `max_count` caps the matches returned. It matches words, not meaning: a question worded differently from the documents is knowledge_search's.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the file to read. Must be absolute, not relative.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read. Use for pagination of large files.

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (0-indexed). Use for pagination of large files.

tool:chat:ask_user.description:
Ask the user ONE multiple-choice question in the middle of your answer and WAIT for their pick, then continue this same turn using what they chose. The user sees your question with the options as selectable buttons.

WHEN TO USE IT. Whenever you can already name a SMALL, ENUMERABLE set of 2-6 concrete options and picking the wrong one would meaningfully change the answer: the two IFC models in the project, the three Bundesländer the question could mean, the two document versions that both match, or several genuinely distinct ways to read an ambiguous question. You must be able to name the options yourself — if you cannot list them, this is not the tool. Prefer asking over silently guessing whenever the options would lead to different answers; a good one-shot question here is what makes the rest of the answer trustworthy instead of a guess.

WHEN NOT TO USE IT. Do NOT ask for something a search or another tool could establish: look it up instead, that is what the tools are for. Do NOT ask for something the project context already states. Do NOT ask when the choice would NOT meaningfully change the answer, or when a stated assumption is just as good — then answer, and say which assumption you made ("Ich gehe von Bauklasse 4 aus; für eine andere Klasse gilt …"). At most ONE ask_user per turn. Never for an open question ("welcher Zeitraum?") — write those as prose in your answer instead.
