      GFZ). A pure density question leaves `sides` empty; a limit the Bebauungsplan did not give
      you stays out.
  a barrier-free lift: cabin width, cabin depth, door -> dimension_diagram
      shape `lift_cabin`, with Kabinenbreite, Kabinentiefe and lichte Türbreite as its dimensions.
      Whether a lift is required at all is a sentence with its Fundstelle, not a field.
  a number the answer WORKED OUT rather than looked up, other than the four rules of the row below -> calculation
      Supply the operands (label, value, unit) and the rule's limit; the card computes, rounds and
      judges, and there is no result field, on purpose. The rule's multiplier is a `factor`, never
      a second operand, and an operand you do not have stays empty — the card renders „nicht
      berechenbar". Never for a number merely cited: one operand is the sentence beside it, typeset
      twice.
  a U-value from its layers, the Schrittmaßregel, an escape route's Gehweglänge, or a Lichteintrittsfläche against the Bodenfläche -> formula
      Name the rule and its case (`stair_type`, `component` and `measure`, `start`) and fill each
      input from a source, with `source` saying where it is written; an input you do not have stays
      null. The card owns the bounds: it reads them from the Richtlinie's table for that case, so
      you write no limit and no figure in the title, a label or the note. It computes, judges and
      lets the reader change the inputs for a what-if, so the prose names the verdict and points at
      the card instead of restating the computed number.
  the user wants to SEE or OPEN the building and the project may hold several models -> ifc_model_picker
      The ifc_model_picker is the answer to "zeig mir das Modell" / "welches Modell soll ich
      öffnen": emit it INSTEAD of writing the file names as a prose bullet list. It renders the
      project's models as tiles the user clicks to open the viewer directly — you supply only the
      heading, never the file names, so there is nothing to get wrong. You do not need to call
      ifc_query first to list them.

WHAT MAY GO ON ONE. Never fabricate a field, a reference or a number to fill a card out — a card
with an invented limit in it is worse than the prose alone, because it is the part that gets
screenshotted into a submission. A value you do not have is left out or marked "needs_input", never
estimated to make the card look finished. This rule outranks every trigger above.

WHEN NOT TO. One card is usually the right number, two the ceiling, none the normal case. A
one-line factual answer earns none: the card would only repeat the sentence above it. A card that
shows what a table or a sentence in the prose already shows is a restatement: keep the prose, cut
the card.

HOW. Pass `card_json`: a JSON object with a `type` field plus that type's fields. Fill it from the type's line below and the rules above; you are not shown every shape up front, and you do not need to look one up first — if a field is wrong, the error hands you that type's full shape and a worked example, so an unfamiliar shape is never a reason to skip a card the answer called for. Fields marked * are required; omit optional ones rather than passing null. Numbers are plain JSON numbers. For schematic cards, supply the measured/actual value from the question or project profile and the OIB limit in `required`; if a value is unknown, omit it and set that check's status to "needs_input" — never estimate.

Card types:
  - "project_profile_patch": Propose an update to the project brief (hard project facts) — applied only if the user accepts.
  - "calculation": Emit for the arithmetic behind a number — the Rechenweg a Ziviltechniker re-checks.
  - "formula": Emit for a number worked out by one of four named rules, so the reader can ask "what if" on the card.
  - "building_section": A to-scale building cross-section (schematic) drawn from storey heights.
  - "stair_diagram": A staircase drawn to scale (schematic section) with step-geometry checks.
  - "dimension_diagram": A parametric accessibility/geometry schematic with dimension arrows.
  - "setback_plan": A top-down site plan (schematic): parcel, footprint, setbacks, coverage and GFZ.
  - "egress_diagram": A schematic escape-route (Fluchtweg) path with the total length checked.
  - "daylight_incidence": A daylight (Belichtung) schematic: the 45° free-light line vs obstructions.
  - "guardrail_check": An Absturzsicherung (guardrail) elevation with the interacting limits.
  - "fire_access_plan": A fire-brigade access (Feuerwehrzufahrt) site plan schematic.
  - "ifc_viewer": The project's IFC model, rendered in 3D, with findings highlighted on it.
  - "ifc_compliance": The Prüfbuch: OIB requirements with their verdict against this model.
  - "ifc_schedule": The project's Raumbuch (room schedule) straight from the model.
  - "ifc_element": One element of the model, in full, with a link into the 3D view.
  - "ifc_diff": What changed between two revisions of the model.
  - "ifc_model_picker": A clickable list of the project's IFC models — pick one to open in the viewer.

Cards that ask the user to CONFIRM something ("project_profile_patch"):
  These are not presentation — they ask the user to authorize a real, persisted change, and
  their answer is remembered. Emit one only when you have a SPECIFIC change worth interrupting
  for, grounded in something the user actually said in this conversation. At most one per turn.
  Never emit one speculatively, to ask a question you could ask in prose, or to restate a
  change the user already confirmed.

Batch mode: pass `queries` as either a single string or a list of strings. Each item is run as one underlying source-tool call and returned in grouped sections.

queries.description: One query/input string, or a list of query/input strings.

tool:deep_research.researcher:get_verifi.description:
Returns verified source URLs captured from search tool calls.

Call this tool during synthesis BEFORE writing the final answer. It
returns the compact writer-facing source list by default: sources that
researcher workers carried forward into ResearchNotes. Pass
mode="full" only if a needed ResearchNotes source is missing from the
compact list. Use ONLY returned sources in your final answer. Any
other URL will be automatically removed.

Args:
    mode: "compact" for ResearchNotes-backed sources, or "full" for
        every captured source in the registry.
Returns:
    A numbered list of verified sources with titles and URLs.

tool:deep_research.researcher:ifc_measur.description:
MEASURE the project's IFC/BIM model — geometry, topology and spatial relationships — and report every number with the provenance it came with. Use this when the answer is a DIMENSION, a DISTANCE, an AREA the export may not have published, or a spatial relationship ('which room does this window open into', 'wie hoch ist der Raum wirklich', 'wie weit ist die Tür von der Wand', 'welche Bauteile begrenzen diesen Raum').

This is NOT a replacement for ifc_query. ifc_query reads the extracted index: it is fast, it covers the whole model, and it answers what the export WROTE DOWN — counts, storeys, property values, published quantities. Reach for it first for 'how many' and 'which ones'. Reach for ifc_measure when the file does not state the number and the geometry has to be read, or when a declared number needs a second, independent route to check it against.

CALL 'briefing' FIRST, once per model, before anything else. The briefing is this FILE speaking: it names the storeys with their elevations, the property vocabulary this exporter actually used (DIALEKT), and — the part that saves whole turns — the BLIND section, which says which questions this file cannot answer at all. Storey and property names come from THERE, copied verbatim. A storey name you invented matches nothing, and an empty result reads like 'the building has none'.

What each operation is FOR (the parameters say which arguments it takes):
  'briefing'       — this file speaking about itself. START HERE.
  'find_elements'  — GlobalIds by type, name, storey or spatial role. The input every other operation needs.
  'element'        — everything about ONE element, including which relations it actually has, so a relation that would come back empty need not be guessed at.
  'relations'      — one topological question about one element.
  'measure'        — one measurement of one element, or of an already-known set of them.
  'survey'         — ONE measure across ALL elements of a selection, each named, with the SPREAD over the set. Reach for this the moment the question is plural — 'wie hoch ist der Keller' names one room and means seventeen. Measuring one element and generalising is a guess. The spread IS the finding; report it.
  'element_profile' — the reverse: EVERY measure that applies to ONE element, in one call. Which measures apply follows from the element's IFC type, so a door is not asked for its lichte Raumhöhe. Reach for it once an element has become interesting, such as the outlier a survey named.
  'distance'       — the distance between TWO elements, along an axis, between centroids or boxes. An Achsabstand, never a clear dimension.
  'clearance'      — the LICHTE dimension between TWO elements: the smallest SURFACE-to-SURFACE gap, which 'distance' does not have: its 'min' is a gap between BOUNDING BOXES, a lower bound that lets too tight pass as free. For the clear width of ONE opening use 'measure' with clearWidth instead.
  'sun_position'   — where the sun stood over this building at an instant: azimuth, altitude, and the direction TOWARDS the sun in THIS model's coordinates. NOT a Besonnungsstudie: it says where the sun was, never whether the neighbour's gable was in the way — that needs everything outside the property line, which is not in the file. Undecidable without IfcSite.RefLatitude/RefLongitude; no latitude is assumed, so it takes no coordinates.
  'storey_heights' — the storey pitch (slab top to slab top) for every storey. This is the STRUCTURAL height, NOT the lichte Raumhöhe (that is measure/clearHeight).
  'room_inventory' — rooms grouped by a SUSPECTED use, inferred from their names. A proposal for a human to confirm, never a finding.
  'fire'           — the OIB 2 (Brandschutz) geometry. NO Gebäudeklasse: escape_level returns a HEIGHT, and which class follows from it is a legal classification under OIB 2 plus Landesrecht.
  'envelope'       — the OIB 6 (Wärmeschutz) geometry of the WHOLE building. Asking wall by wall is how the wall that was left out stays invisible, so it takes no element. No U-value is CALCULATED: a declared one is repeated, a missing one stays missing, never derived from the layer set. Costs geometry (seconds).
  'overhang'       — how far one element projects past another's facade plane. The Dachüberstand, the balcony, the canopy.
  'light_incidence' — builds the light prism over an opening's lower edge and reports which elements reach into it and how deep. The result is GEOMETRY: a cut prism enlarges the required Lichteintrittsfläche under OIB 3, it does not ban the window. Report what intrudes and how far, then apply the clause yourself. The host wall is deliberately not excluded on its own, because a window set deep in a thick wall genuinely is shaded by its own reveal — but if the wall comes back as an obstruction, re-run with it excluded (keeping any other exclusion) and say so.
  'view'           — LOOK at a floor plan. Returns the storey as an IMAGE you can actually see, cut at 1.2 m so door and window openings appear as gaps. Use it to settle which element is meant, to sanity-check that a measured arrangement looks the way the numbers imply, or before measuring at all. ~6 s.
  'draw'           — the same floor plan as an SVG FILE for the USER (~5 s). It returns a path, not an image: you cannot see it. Use 'view' when YOU need to look, 'draw' when the user wants the file.
  'shopping_list'  — writes the model's blind spots as a buildingSMART IDS 1.0 file the architect can run in Solibri/BIMcollab/ifctester against their own model. Offer it when several answers came back undecidable, or when asked what to fix in the export. It requires only that a property EXISTS, never its value. The summary names the blind spots it could not express.

PROVENANCE — the reason this tool exists. Every answer says HOW it was obtained, and the three are three different sentences in German that must not be swapped:
  'declared' → „laut Modell …“ / „das Modell deklariert …“. The file states it.
  'computed' → „gemessen: … (±Toleranz)“. WE measured it from the geometry. The tolerance is part of the claim — quote it. NEVER write a computed number as something the model states.
  'inferred' → „vermutlich …“ plus the reasons. A heuristic, offered for confirmation, never a finding. room_inventory is always this: whether a room is an Aufenthaltsraum is a LEGAL classification, not a geometric one.
The rendered summary line already carries the right verb — quote that line rather than reassembling the claim yourself.

'decidable: false' is NOT an error and NOT a fact about the building. It means the question was well formed and THIS EXPORT cannot answer it. Report it as a finding about the export, name what is missing, and pass on 'missing.remedy' verbatim — that sentence is what the architect changes in their CAD to make the question answerable. Saying 'the building has no sill height' when the file merely does not publish one is a wrong answer.

NEVER recompute, round, convert or extrapolate a number this tool returns. Do not add two areas together, do not derive a third dimension from two others, do not restate a millimetre value in centimetres. If a question needs a number that was not returned, make another call — arithmetic done in an answer is a guess wearing the tool's authority. And NEVER read a measurement off a drawing ('view' or 'draw'): a value read off an image is guessed even when it happens to be right.

COST — plan the calls before making them. 'briefing', 'find_elements' and 'element' are free (pure topology). The first 'measure' or 'distance' on a model tessellates it (~2 s for a single-family house). The relations marked [geometry] cost seconds on a cold model: opensTo, bounds, enclosedBy and adjacentSpaces build a space-contact map on first use (about 7 s), because most exports write no IfcRelSpaceBoundary. After that everything is milliseconds. Do NOT call the geometric relations speculatively — call them when the answer needs them.

A typical chain ('ist die Raumhöhe im Wohnzimmer ausreichend?'): operation='briefing'; operation='find_elements' ifc_type='IfcSpace' name_contains='Wohn' storey='<from the briefing>'; operation='measure' measure='clearHeight' on that GlobalId, or operation='survey' on the whole storey; report the rendered line as it stands.

When the model cannot be resolved the tool says so in German — report that sentence rather than answering from your own knowledge of buildings.

A measurement that contradicts a declared quantity is reported as a contradiction ('Widerspruch'), and that is a FINDING an architect wants before submission: their schedule and their geometry disagree. Report both numbers and which one the tool preferred; do not silently pick one.

angle_deg.description: 'light_incidence' only — the Lichteinfallswinkel in degrees, strictly between 0 and 90. It is a fact about the BESTIMMUNG, not the model (OIB 3: 45, with swivel_deg 30), so the tool refuses without it rather than defaulting.

global_id.description: The element's IFC GlobalId, from 'find_elements', 'element' or an ifc_query result in THIS turn; an invented id is refused. Usually ONE id. A list (or one comma-separated string) where the question is about a set: 'measure' over an already-known selection (at most 50, each element keeping its own answer, tolerance and refusal), 'view' to mark several at once, 'fire' with kind='compartmentArea' for the rooms of the compartment, exactly two rooms for kind='separatingElements'. The selecting and whole-model operations ('find_elements', 'survey', 'draw', 'envelope') take none.

ifc_type.description: 'find_elements', 'survey' and 'draw' — the IFC CLASS, e.g. IfcSpace, IfcWindow, IfcDoor. The spatial role goes in 'kind' instead.

kind.description:
Three vocabularies on one field, scoped by operation.
  'find_elements' and 'survey' — the spatial ROLE, not the IFC type (a room is 'space'): project, site, building, storey, space, element, opening, group.
  'fire' — which OIB 2 (Brandschutz) geometry, default 'escape_level':
    escape_level — height of the topmost occupied floor above the lowest adjoining ground — the number the Gebäudeklasse hangs on. Returns a HEIGHT and never a class
    compartmentArea — floor area of a fire compartment across several rooms, each room listed
    separatingElements — what lies BETWEEN two rooms — wall, slab, and the doors in them — each with its DECLARED FireRating, and explicitly with its absence
    siteBoundary — distance to the site boundary (Brandübertragung). Undecidable on most exports, because a parcel boundary is rarely exported — and it is not guessed here
    doorGraph — the WHOLE building's walkable graph: rooms as nodes, OUTSIDE as its own node, doors as edges, plus the doors that became NEITHER (unbestimmt, ausgeschlossen). A room with no edge has no way out; an unresolved door is a hole in every route. Takes no global_id
  'envelope' — which OIB 6 (Wärmeschutz) geometry of the WHOLE building, default 'thermalEnvelope':
    thermalEnvelope — which elements form the boundary between heated inside and outside, grouped by kind, each with its area, its DECLARED U-value and which rung decided it (declared IsExternal or inferred from room contact), plus interior (decided, left out) and unbestimmt (neither counted nor discarded)
    areaByOrientation — envelope area per compass bearing, opaque and transparent apart, with the window-to-wall ratio per facade. Needs a declared TrueNorth; without one the bearing is refused, not guessed
    compactness — A/V in 1/m, with the characteristic length (V over A), and A and V separately. V is the NET volume (the sum of the IfcSpace solids)
  'element_profile' — 'expensive' to include escape route, reachability, turning circle and door approach, which are left out otherwise.
Unused by every other operation.

limit.description: How many rows: 'find_elements' up to 500, 'survey' up to 50. 0 leaves the server's default.

measure.description:
'measure' (one element) and 'survey' (a whole selection) — WHICH quantity:
    extent — width, depth, height and centroid of one element
    floorArea — a room's floor area FROM THE GEOMETRY, even when the export publishes none; a published one is compared and a contradiction reported
    sillAndHead — Brüstungs- und Sturzhöhe of a window/door above ITS OWN storey
    elevation — underside and top, absolute and above the element's own storey
    clearHeight — lichte Raumhöhe — floor to the LOWEST thing hanging into the room (suspended ceiling, downstand, duct). NOT the height of the space solid ('extent'), which a Raumhöhennachweis must not use
    azimuth — which way a facade faces. Undecidable without TrueNorth in the file
    lightEntryArea — a ROOM's light-entry area and what percent of its floor area that is — the number an OIB 3 daylight check comes down to. Sums only the EXTERNAL openings (an internal door lights nothing) and measures the structural clear opening, not the glazed area. Applies no threshold: the percentage is in the Bestimmung, not in the model
    egressPath — a ROOM's shortest WALKABLE route to the outside through doors (adjacency is not walkability), with the rooms, the doors and a length. The length runs through room and door centres, so it is a LOWER BOUND and not a Fluchtweglänge
    reachableFrom — every room reachable from this one through doors, with door counts. Answers 'which rooms are behind this door', and finds rooms with no way out at all — itself a finding
    clearWidth — the LICHTE Breite and Höhe of an opening, measured on the aperture itself. THIS is what a door-width or escape-route-width check needs
    orientedExtent — length/width/height along the ELEMENT's own axes plus its bearing from north. Use for anything skewed to the model grid, where 'extent' is axis-aligned and systematically too large
    roomDepth — how deep a room runs back from its daylight facade, the width along that facade, and the ratio to the clear height. Names which facade it chose and, for a corner room, the runner-up
    stairGeometry — riser height, tread depth, riser count and the NUTZBREITE of a stair flight, plus the SPREAD of the risers. Declared values are checked against the geometry and a contradiction reported
    rampSlope — a ramp's slope as a percentage AND as a ratio, with run, rise and clear width
    headroom — clear height over a stair flight or ramp, measured PERPENDICULAR to the pitch, not vertically
    stepsOf — the flights and landings a stair is made of, so one flight can be asked about
    turningCircle — the largest circle that fits on a ROOM's free floor, for a Wendekreis check. Counts fixed built-ins only; furniture is reported beside it. Applies no threshold
    thresholdHeight — the step at a door. Where the export models no floor build-up this is a STRUCTURAL number, which says nothing about the finished threshold, and the answer says so
    balustrade — where there is a fall at an opening, how far, and what stands there. Undecidable when the export contains no IfcRailing at all
    clearApproach — the free floor in front of a door on each side, and what ends it

mode.description:
Two vocabularies on one field, scoped by operation.
  'distance' (default 'min'):
    min — gap between the two axis-aligned BOUNDING BOXES. 0 means the boxes overlap — it does NOT prove the solids touch, and on a skewed element the true gap is larger
    centroid — centre to centre in 3D (Achsabstand). NOT a clear dimension
    horizontal — centre to centre in plan, Z ignored (Achsabstand) — what a plan drawing scales off. NOT a lichte Breite: for a clear width use measure/clearWidth on the opening
    vertical — difference in centre HEIGHT — what a section scales off. NOT a lichte Höhe: for that use measure/clearHeight on the room
  NONE of those four is a clear dimension: use operation='clearance' for the smallest surface-to-surface gap.
  'view' (default 'highlight'):
    highlight — mark these elements red on the full plan — 'where is this in the building'
    only — draw nothing but these elements — 'what does this look like'
Unused by every other operation.

model_name.description: A substring of the file name, to pick one model when the project has several. Leave it empty when there is only one.

name_contains.description: 'find_elements' and 'survey' — a substring of the element's name. Take it from the briefing or from an earlier result; an invented fragment matches nothing.

operation.description: WHICH question to ask. The only required argument — every other field is scoped by this one. On a model you have not looked at yet, 'briefing'.

other_global_id.description: The SECOND element, and it means a different thing per operation. 'distance' and 'clearance': the element to measure against. 'overhang': the element whose outer face is the REFERENCE plane, while global_id is the projecting one (get it from relations/hostedIn on the window). 'light_incidence': the elements EXCLUDED from the test — a list, or several ids separated by commas. Unused by every other operation.

relation.description:
'relations' only — which topological question to ask about global_id:
    hostedIn — which wall carries this window/door (from voids+fills)
    hosts — which openings are cut out of this element
    fillerOf — what fills this opening
    bounds — which elements bound this room  [geometry]
    enclosedBy — which rooms this element bounds  [geometry]
    opensTo — which rooms this window/door opens into  [geometry]
    connects — which elements butt onto this one
    contains — which elements sit in this storey or room
    containerOf — which storey or room this element sits in
    adjacentSpaces — which rooms border this room  [geometry]
    elementsOfStorey — every element of this storey, including those in rooms
    above — what is directly ABOVE this element or room  [geometry, rays; furniture excluded]
    below — what is directly BELOW it  [geometry, rays]

room_kind.description: 'room_inventory' only — which SUSPECTED use to group the rooms by.

storey.description: 'find_elements', 'survey', 'draw' and 'view' — the storey name EXACTLY as the briefing spells it.

swivel_deg.description: 'light_incidence' only — the lateral Verschwenkung in degrees, from 0 to under 90. From the Bestimmung as well (OIB 3: 30).

when.description: 'sun_position' only — an ISO 8601 instant WITH a time zone, e.g. '2026-06-21T12:00:00+02:00' or '2026-06-21T10:00:00Z'. A timestamp without a zone is refused rather than read as UTC.

tool:deep_research.researcher:ifc_query.description:
Query the project's IFC/BIM model for EXACT facts about the building: element counts, rooms and their areas, storeys, property values (fire rating, U-value, load-bearing, …), materials and classifications. Use this INSTEAD of knowledge_search whenever the question is about THIS building rather than about a regulation — 'how many escape doors', 'net floor area per storey', 'which walls are external', 'what is the U-value of the windows'.

An IFC model is a TREE: project → site → building → storey → elements, and rooms are IfcSpace elements sitting in a storey. 'which storey is this on' and 'which rooms are in the Erdgeschoss' are answered by that containment, not by geometry.

operation:
  'overview'   — what the model is: project/site/building names, storeys, totals, areas. Start here when you do not yet know what the model contains.
  'health'     — the model's VALIDATION report: elements assigned to no storey, rooms with no published area, duplicated GlobalIds, missing standard property sets. Read this before making a claim about model coverage, and never present a model as complete without it.
  'types'      — element counts per IFC type (IfcWall: 128, IfcDoor: 34, …).
  'properties' — the model's OWN property vocabulary: which property sets exist, which properties they carry, and the values those properties actually take, with counts. ALWAYS call this before filtering on a property you have not seen — guessing a plausible property name returns zero rows, which reads like 'the building has none'.
  'elements'   — list matching elements (name, type, storey, tag).
  'element'    — everything about ONE element, addressed by its IFC GlobalId.
  'schedule'   — the Raumbuch: every room with its storey, area and volume, plus the per-storey and building totals. Use for 'Flächenaufstellung', 'welche Räume', 'wie groß ist'. The totals already say how many rooms publish no area — report that too.
  'takeoff'    — Massenermittlung: one quantity summed per element type, optionally split by material. Set 'quantity' (NetSideArea, NetVolume, …) and group_by="material" for a cost-estimate breakdown. The material split matches the material NAMES the export wrote (a substring match on names like 'Beton C25/30'); it does not read the layer structure, so a wall counts once under its first material rather than per layer.
  'profile'    — project facts the MODEL implies: storeys above/below ground, the Fluchtniveau band, the main use. These are PROPOSALS with their evidence — offer them through a project_profile_patch card for the user to confirm, never state them as settled.
  'compliance' — run the OIB rule catalogue against the model and report, per requirement, how many elements are met / not met / UNDECIDABLE (the model does not publish the value, NOT that the building fails). Each row names the exact property (e.g. Pset_WallCommon.FireRating) that would settle it — report that list, it is what the architect has to add in their CAD. Pass building_class and main_use from the project data when you know them; a rule that needs a fact it was not given stands down WITH its reason rather than guessing. main_use must be one of residential, office, lodging, assembly, healthcare, agriculture, manufacturing, storage, other — anything else makes rules stand down as 'not applicable', which reads as a verdict and is not one. building_class is 1-5.
  'compliance-diff' — the same catalogue over two revisions, reporting only the requirements whose STATUS MOVED. Set 'compare_with' to a substring of the OLDER file's name. This answers 'was hat sich der letzte Stand kaputt gemacht', including a requirement that stopped being decidable.
  'compare'    — what changed between TWO revisions of the same building. Set 'compare_with' to a substring of the OLDER file's name; this model is the newer one. Matched by IFC GlobalId. Use it for 'what changed since the last submission'.
  'aggregate'  — count/sum/avg/min/max over the matching elements, optionally grouped by ifcType, storey, predefinedType, typeName or material. This is how you answer 'how many' and 'how much' — never add up an element list yourself.

filters (JSON object, all optional): {"ifcTypes": ["IfcWall"], "storeys": ["Erdgeschoss"], "nameContains": "Flucht", "material": "Beton", "classification": "B.1.2", "properties": [{"set": "Pset_WallCommon", "name": "IsExternal", "operator": "eq", "value": true}]}. Property operators: eq, neq, contains, gt, gte, lt, lte, exists, missing. 'set' may be omitted to search every property set. Use "source": "quantity" inside a property filter to match a quantity instead.

STOREY NAMES are matched exactly, and exports name storeys whatever the modeller typed ('EG', '00 Erdgeschoss', 'Level 0'). Call 'overview' first and copy the storey names it returns verbatim; any other name matches nothing, and an empty result reads like 'the ground floor has no walls'.

Every filter key is validated. An unknown key is REJECTED, not ignored — if the tool says a key was not recognised, fix the spelling and call again rather than reporting the result of a query that never ran. Only 'elements', 'aggregate' and 'takeoff' take filters at all; the rest read the whole model and refuse one rather than quietly answering a wider question.

If a result says its figures cover only PART of the model, say so in the answer. Those are not the building's totals and must not be presented as such.

For aggregate: metric is count (default), sum, avg, min or max; sum/avg/min/max need 'quantity' (e.g. NetFloorArea, NetSideArea, NetVolume). groupBy is optional. sum and avg SKIP elements that do not publish the quantity, and the summary says so as 'über X von Y Bauteilen' — report both numbers.

Never turn a compliance result into a statement that the building complies. The catalogue is an orienting check (orientierende Prüfung) over the values the model publishes, it reads no geometry, and escape-route lengths, parapet heights and fire-compartment sizes are not in it at all. Say what was checked, what was not, and what could not be decided.

Report the caveat line verbatim whenever one comes back: it says which parts of the building the numbers do NOT cover.

A missing value is a fact about the EXPORT, not about the building. IFC2X3 models in particular rarely publish Qto_* quantity sets at all, so 'no NetFloorArea' on a 2X3 file usually means the exporter did not write quantities — not that the rooms have no area. Check 'overview' for the schema version and say which of the two it is rather than reporting zero.

Whenever a row comes back with a 'Link:' value, the path is data: copy it verbatim if you name that element in a sentence. Never invent a path.

How a query becomes a card is `ifc-spatial-reasoning`, not this description. Load that skill before emitting a model card. Highlight a set with the same filter that found it, rather than a list of ids. A highlight group takes exactly one of the two per group.

When a compliance result comes back with a 'BCF export of the open issues:' path, OFFER it as a link at the end of the answer — `[offene Punkte als BCF](/api/projects/…/bim/checks/export?…)` using that exact path. It downloads the open requirements as a BCF 2.1 file that opens in ArchiCAD, Revit, Solibri or BIMcollab with the affected elements selected. The export is ONE-WAY: nothing reads the topics back, so a resolved item shows up here only after the corrected model is re-uploaded and checked again — say that rather than implying the BCF tracks status.

model_name selects one model when the project has several (a substring of the file name); leave it empty when there is only one. Report the numbers this tool returns as they are — do not recompute, round differently, or extrapolate them.

tool:deep_research.researcher:knowledge_.description:
Searches the ingested knowledge base (the office's files and the OIB corpus) and returns quotable passages, each with a Citation key: the evidence tool. It does not put a file on screen (`surface_documents` does).
Inputs: `query`, a search query in the documents' language (topic, jurisdiction, year), not the raw user message. Narrow with `file_name=` (an indexed name from the inventory or the user; never invent one), `folder=` (a path as the inventory prints it after 'Ordner:'; includes everything filed beneath it; never invent one), `doc_class=` (Dokumentart key, e.g. oib_guideline), `title_contains=`, and `shelf=` (project, office or base; omitted, every shelf is read), or with `path=` as a hit's `Path:` line names a place, a folder or one file. `group_by="document"` (ranked search only) returns one entry per document: its best passage and how many passages of the ranked pool it held.
`match="exact"` returns EVERY passage that contains the query literally, plus a table of the matching files with count and pages, and shows a term is written nowhere. Several spellings go in one query separated by '|'; case, ä/ae, ß/ss and a line break, space or hyphen between words are matched for you; a term of two or three characters matches as a whole word only. `stemmed=true` also finds inflected forms. Per shelf it states how many documents were searched and how many matched.
`match="regex"` is the same search with a regex in Python syntax, case-insensitive, for a pattern (a Geschäftszahl `MA 37/\d{6}`, a fire door `\bT30-\d+`); `|` is then regex alternation. It needs one literal whole word or number it must contain (`37`, `T30`), or a `folder=`, `file_name=` or `doc_class=` to read in; a pattern that backtracks is refused. `context=` (0 to 3) adds the lines around every hit. A search that stops at its limit says so, and its counts are then lower bounds.
Returns: numbered passages with Source, Citation (cite this key verbatim), Dokumentart, Ordner, page and text. A query that names a Richtlinie and nothing else ('OIB 2') returns every part of it the corpus holds, each with its Geltungsbereich and Gliederung: every member is then open at the level a read of one document opens it, and what is left to open is a Punkt by number.
`conclusion=`: Optional: one line on what you are looking for, shown to the person. No effect on the result. Returns up to 16 excerpts by default (platform-configurable up to 50; the result header counts them), spread across multiple distinct documents (at most 5 per document where possible), so cross-cutting questions see every relevant Richtlinie.

tool:deep_research.researcher:list_files.description:
Lists the reader's OWN files the way the Files pane shows them: which files exist, in which folder, of which Dokumentart, uploaded when. A deterministic listing, paged, not capped by the prompt inventory. It says which files exist, not what they say: reading or searching the documents does.
Inputs, all optional: with none, every file on Projektwissen, Büroablage and Private Sitzung, ordered by folder, after an overview of the top-level folders with file counts. `folder=` one folder and everything below it. `name_contains=` words that must all appear in the file name or title (case and umlaut spelling do not matter). `doc_class=` a Dokumentart key. `added_since=` YYYY-MM-DD. `sort=newest`. `topic=` a Thema recognised in the documents (Attika, Holzrahmenbau). `shelf=` project | office_shelf | session | base (base, the platform OIB corpus, is listed only when asked). `offset=` the next page, as the result says.
`view="tree"` (`depth=` 1-4, default 2) returns a card per folder instead of file lines: counts, Dokumentart mix, pages, dates, the current Fassung; filters apply, no paging.
`revisions_of=` a file name returns that document's whole chain of Fassungen, newest first, each with Index/Datum, upload date and what changed against the one before; every other filter is ignored. With `compare_to=` another Fassung of the chain (its file name, or "previous"), it returns what changed, page by page, in the printed text and in the reading of the drawings, with the Plankopf's Index and Stand („was hat sich zwischen Index B und C geändert“). `compare_to=` may also name any other file of the reader that is no Fassung of it („vergleiche die Raumliste mit dem Raumprogramm“): the two are then compared as two different documents, first → second. Either way, tables and lists (xlsx, csv, tables in a PDF) are compared row by row, matched by the column that identifies a row, and each deviating row names its place in both files.
Returns: a count, the subfolders, then one line per file: exact file name, title, folder, Dokumentart, page count, topics, the date a photo was taken, a Fassung mark (read from the name, or a replacement a person confirmed, with what changed), upload date, a one-line summary. An index, not a source: it is never cited, and a summary does not say what a file contains. File names are written exactly as returned; each becomes a link the reader can open.

tool:deep_research.researcher:look.description: Shows you a page of a document as an image; with `region=[x, y, w, h]` only that box, sharper. `document`: the file name from the inventory or from a hit's `Citation:` line, or a document id; empty means the document open on the canvas, then this chat's document. `page` starts at 1. `region` is shares of the page as shown: 0 to 1, origin top left, never pixels. `image_index` shows the embedded image a hit's `Image:` line names, at its own resolution; a hit's `Region:` line gives the numbers for the place it sits. Where something lies on a sheet is read off the image, not off the text. `question` (optional): a second reader, the office's vision model, answers it from the same crop as short lines starting `Gelesen:`, a reading of the drawing and never a measurement; a reading does not cost a look. A look's result carries its `[N]` to cite. A look that finds nothing is reported as absence in the prose, not shown as a card. At most 6 looks per turn, at most 2 of them whole pages; every result says how many are left. Fails open with a sentence saying why.

tool:deep_research.researcher:read_passa.description:
Opens a document by name: `document=` alone returns its OUTLINE, the document's opening passage plus a Gliederung of its top-level Punkte, and `document=` with `clause=` or `page=` returns exactly that passage. A lookup, not a search: no ranking, and it cannot find a document from a topic (`knowledge_search` does).
Inputs: `document`, the exact name or display title as the inventory or a hit printed it (e.g. 'OIB-Richtlinie 2, Ausgabe Mai 2023' or 'oib-rl_2_ausgabe_mai_2023.pdf'). `clause`, the number alone ('3.5.2', no 'Pkt.') or a table's caption ('Tabelle 3'), or for a project document what a hit's `Punkt:` line printed ('§ 4', 'Zeilen 2-41'); with `clause=`, `page=` is ignored. `page`, one page number. `pages`, a range ('4-6', at most 30 pages) in reading order without the overlap between neighbouring chunks, up to about 6k tokens; a read that stopped early ends with a `cursor` to pass back with the same `document=`.
Returns: the passages, each with Source, Citation (copy verbatim), Dokumentart, Punkt and page. The Gliederung is an index, not evidence: only passages carry a Citation; a Punkt it lists, or one an outline in a `knowledge_search` result lists, opens here by its number (`clause=`). An unknown document name is refused, with up to three labelled guesses from this turn's readable inventory when anything is close.
`conclusion=` is optional: one line on what you are looking for; it has no effect on the call.

tool:deep_research.researcher:remember.description:
Record ONE durable finding in long-term memory, for future conversations. First decide whom the finding is ABOUT: that decides 'scope', and 'scope' decides who reads it. About the PERSON asking: 'personal', also in a project conversation. About the PROJECT: 'project', the default. A firm-wide convention for ALL projects: 'organization'. Never put a finding about a person into project or organization memory. When you cannot tell whether a preference is the person's or the team's, it is the person's: use scope 'personal'.
Do NOT record general building-code knowledge, transient conversation details, restatements of the person's message, facts already in the project profile, or secrets (passwords, keys, account or identity numbers).
When a project finding CORRECTS an entry of the PROJECT_MEMORY shown in your context, pass the outdated entry's text VERBATIM as 'supersedes', which retires it. The same for PERSONAL_MEMORY with scope 'personal': when the person asks you to drop, undo or forget a personal note, pass its text as 'supersedes' and leave 'content' empty, which removes it. Never record a note that contradicts or negates an earlier one in its place.
Only tell the person it was noted when the result says it was recorded.

confidence.description: How certain the finding is: 'low', 'medium' or 'high'. Not used with scope 'personal'.

content.description: The finding as ONE concise, self-contained sentence that can be understood without this conversation, in the language the person wrote in. With scope 'personal', never the person's name and never the third person: only that person reads it, so state the preference or role itself, e.g. 'Maße immer in Zentimetern.' or 'Im Büro für Brandschutz zuständig.' Empty only to remove a personal note named in 'supersedes'.

kind.description: What the finding is. Scope 'project' or 'organization': 'decision' (a choice the client or the team made), 'constraint' (a requirement imposed on the project), 'open_question' (unresolved, to follow up), 'derived_fact' (a concluded property of the project), 'preference' (how the TEAM wants the assistant to work). Scope 'personal': 'preference' (how this person wants the assistant to work) or 'profile' (their role, responsibilities, recurring topics, something said in confidence).

scope.description: Whose memory, chosen by whom the finding is ABOUT, never by where the conversation takes place. 'personal': about the person asking; only that person reads it. 'project': about the current project; the project's members read it. 'organization': holds for every project of the organization; everyone in the organization reads it.

supersedes.description: The verbatim text of the memory entry this finding corrects, without its tag and without the surrounding quotes: a PROJECT_MEMORY entry for scope 'project' or 'organization', a PERSONAL_MEMORY entry for scope 'personal'. Empty when the finding adds something new. With scope 'personal' and an empty 'content', the entry is removed and nothing is recorded.

topic.description: The subject the note is filed under: one to three words in the person's language, a subject not a kind (e.g. 'fire safety', not 'decision'). Reuse a topic already shown in memory when one fits. Empty if none.

tool:deep_research.researcher:ris_catalo.description:
Look up an Austrian building-law topic in the curated RIS catalog of verified norms.

WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
- Any question about Austrian building law: Bauordnungen,
  Bautechnikgesetze/-verordnungen, and the adjacent federal acts. The catalog
  maps topics to VERIFIED RIS pointers (application, document number, citation
  URL, 'entire consolidated law' URL) - no keyword guessing, no wrong silo.
- What it returns is an ADDRESS per norm, never the text at it and never a
  requirement: a pointer is not a provision and cannot be cited as one.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- The catalog covers only the core building-relevant norms. For case law,
  draft bills, gazettes, or anything beyond it, use ris_search (live RIS search).

Args:
    topic (str): German building-law topic. ALWAYS name the Bundesland for
        state-law topics (e.g. "Bauordnung Tirol", "Stellplatz Wien") — the
        nine state building codes differ, and the lookup returns the named
        state's law (plus federal law) instead of all nine.

Returns:
    str: Verified pointer blocks (application, document number, citation URL,
        entire-law URL) or guidance to use ris_search when nothing matches.

Batch mode: pass `queries` as either a single string or a list of strings. Each item is run as one underlying source-tool call and returned in grouped sections.

queries.description: One query/input string, or a list of query/input strings.

tool:deep_research.researcher:ris_fetch_.description:
Fetch the ENTIRE text of an Austrian law or court decision from RIS on demand.

WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
- You hold a RIS ADDRESS — a document number or a ris.bka.gv.at URL — and need the text
  at it. A reference is not quotable; this is what turns one into a document.
- To load a complete consolidated law (every paragraph) from its 'Entire consolidated law'
  URL, e.g. for a question spanning several sections.
- To re-read a document the user or an earlier step referenced.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- For documents not hosted on ris.bka.gv.at (this tool only fetches RIS).
- When the relevant text is already fully present in this conversation.

The fetched document is also added to the session knowledge base (full text, not truncated),
so knowledge_search can retrieve and cite specific sections in later steps.

Args:
    reference (str): RIS document number from ris_search (e.g. "NOR40217157",
        "JWT_2020130074_20210415J00") or any https://www.ris.bka.gv.at/... URL from
        ris_search results (document URL or 'Entire consolidated law' URL).
    application (str): Only needed with a document number whose application cannot be
        inferred: "BrKons", "LrKons", "Vfgh", "Vwgh", "Justiz", "Bvwg", "Lvwg", ...

Returns:
    str: The document's full text (truncated if very long) with its citation URL,
        retrieval date, and legal-status note.

tool:deep_research.researcher:ris_search.description:
Search the official Austrian legal information system RIS — the authoritative, always-current
source for Austrian federal law, state law, and court decisions.

WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
- The question turns on what an Austrian law, regulation, or court actually SAYS: exact
  wording, scope, thresholds, obligations, penalties, validity, or applicable version.
- You need the precise legal anchor behind a requirement (law name, paragraph, Bundesland,
  version). OIB-Richtlinien become binding via the state building laws found here.
- Building law: Bauordnungen, Bautechnikgesetze, and Garagengesetze are STATE law — search
  application "LrKons" and always set the federal_state.
- Case law: how courts interpreted a provision (Vfgh, Vwgh, Justiz, Bvwg, Lvwg).

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- Content of the OIB-Richtlinien themselves or user-uploaded documents → knowledge_search.
- Non-Austrian law, news, products, or general facts → web search.

This returns document REFERENCES — title, application, document number, citation URL —
and never the wording of a provision. Nothing here is quotable: a reference is an address,
and a legal answer is grounded in the document that address names.

Args:
    query (str): German legal search terms, e.g. "Stellplatzverpflichtung Garage". Use
        statutory terminology, not colloquial phrasing.
    application (str): RIS application: "BrKons" consolidated federal law (default),
        "LrKons" consolidated state law, "BgblAuth" authentic federal gazette, "Begut"
        draft bills, "RegV" government bills, "Vfgh"/"Vwgh"/"Justiz"/"Bvwg"/"Lvwg" case
        law, "Dsk" data protection decisions, "Erlaesse" ministry decrees.
    title (str): Optional title filter when a specific law is named, e.g. "Bauordnung für Wien".
    federal_state (str): State filter for state-law searches ("Wien", "Tirol", ...). Required
        practice for Bauordnung questions.
    date_from (str): Optional YYYY-MM-DD. Case law: earliest decision date. "BrKons": the
        version in force at this date.
    date_to (str): Optional YYYY-MM-DD. Case law: latest decision date.
    page (int): 1-based result page.

Returns:
    str: Numbered document references with citation URLs and fetch instructions.

tool:deep_research.researcher:surface_do.description:
Show the user a REAL project or Büroablage FILE in the UI (preview card). This is not a citation tool — it does not return quotable passages.
WHEN TO CALL — the user asked to SEE or BROWSE their own files, with no legal question to answer. Examples: 'zeig mir den Brandschutzplan', 'öffne Schnitt.pdf', 'welche Unterlagen habe ich zu Fluchtwegen'.
- `filename=` the exact indexed name (inventory or the user) when they named a file. Opens that one file.
- `mode=one` (default) + `query=` when they asked to see the best matching file and you do not have the name. Opens one file. Not a follow-up to a citation.
- `mode=many` + `query=` only when they are choosing among two or three NEARLY EQUALLY relevant files of the same kind. Never a catalogue, never the inventory.
- `shelf=office_shelf` / `shelf=project` when they asked to see files on ONE shelf (Büroablage vs this project). Do not mix the two.
Asking for files of a KIND ('hab ich sonst noch Grundrisse', 'welche Fotos vom Bestand') is a browse: `mode=many` on that shelf, so they can open them.
WHEN NOT TO CALL — to say what is on a shelf ('welche Dateien hast du im Büroablage'), answer from the knowledge-base inventory, or from a listing where the inventory is incomplete or the question filters by folder, name or date; file names written in the answer already open on click. To read, quote, or cite a passage, use `knowledge_search`. The UI already peeks the cited file; do not also call this tool after citing. Do not use this for OIB / RIS / web questions.
Never invent filenames. After a successful call, talk about the file in prose; do not dump a filename list.

tool:deep_research.researcher:think.description: Use this tool to reason through decisions, verify constraints, or plan next steps.

tool:deep_research.source_router:lookup_.description: Return configured source domains, available source IDs, and exact source tool names.

tool:intake.lookups:classification_evalu.description: The building's class under its site's rules, open inputs, and the document for each.

planned.description: Planned values by fact key, to try a variant.

tool:intake.lookups:project_base_get.description: The project's base knowledge: the gate (site_unknown, not_entitled, or coverage), the chain, every edition with its role, and the procedures.

tool:intake.lookups:site_resolve.description: Resolve a typed address against the official register: country, Land, municipality.

q.description: The address as typed, e.g. 'Herrengasse 16, 8010 Graz'.

tool:intake:finish_intake.description: End the reading: tell the intake API it is done, with your summary, and stop. Call it when the needs are covered, when the documents hold nothing more for them, or when the budget is spent. Nothing runs after it. While decisive needs are open and files are unread, the first call does not finish: it names them, and a second call finishes as it is. The summary is shown to the person who checks the reading and is handed to the next reading of this project as its starting note: every claim in it rests on something a tool returned in this run (files read, values recorded, refusals), and it says plainly what stays open and which document would answer it.

summary.description: Two to four German sentences for the person who checks the reading: what you read, what you found, what stays open and which document would answer it. At most 2000 characters.

tool:intake:intake_needs.description: What the project's profile still needs, from the intake API, as it stands now: every question the wizard would ask for what is known (key, label, type, option tokens, unit, where the value is usually found, why it is asked), and the files no reading has read yet. `decisive`: filling it could change a Bauwerk's building class. State `open`: nothing on the profile. `suggested`: a document's value is there, unconfirmed; record it again only from another document, which corroborates it or, if different, is kept beside it for a person. `confirmed`: a person confirmed a building-class input; record it only from a document that states it (a newer Stand, say): the same value corroborates it, a different one becomes a contradiction a person decides, and the confirmed value is never overwritten. Answers change as values are recorded: a recorded value can open new questions (Nutzungen open the Wohnungen of a Wohnbau). A key you know from the documents need not be listed yet to be recorded: any key a wizard question writes is taken. Bounded at 60 needs per answer; `start` pages on.

start.description: Skip this many needs: the answer names the next start when bounded.

Lists the reader's OWN files the way the Files pane shows them: which files exist, in which folder, of which Dokumentart, uploaded when. A deterministic listing, paged, not capped by the prompt inventory. It says which files exist, not what they say: reading or searching the documents does.
Inputs, all optional: with none, every file on Projektwissen, Büroablage and Private Sitzung, ordered by folder, after an overview of the top-level folders with file counts. `folder=` one folder and everything below it. `name_contains=` words that must all appear in the file name or title (case and umlaut spelling do not matter). `doc_class=` a Dokumentart key. `added_since=` YYYY-MM-DD. `sort=newest`. `topic=` a Thema recognised in the documents (Attika, Holzrahmenbau). `shelf=` project | office_shelf | session | base (base, the platform OIB corpus, is listed only when asked). `offset=` the next page, as the result says.
`view="tree"` (`depth=` 1-4, default 2) returns a card per folder instead of file lines: counts, Dokumentart mix, pages, dates, the current Fassung; filters apply, no paging.
`revisions_of=` a file name returns that document's whole chain of Fassungen, newest first, each with Index/Datum, upload date and what changed against the one before; every other filter is ignored. With `compare_to=` another Fassung of the chain (its file name, or "previous"), it returns what changed, page by page, in the printed text and in the reading of the drawings, with the Plankopf's Index and Stand („was hat sich zwischen Index B und C geändert“). `compare_to=` may also name any other file of the reader that is no Fassung of it („vergleiche die Raumliste mit dem Raumprogramm“): the two are then compared as two different documents, first → second. Either way, tables and lists (xlsx, csv, tables in a PDF) are compared row by row, matched by the column that identifies a row, and each deviating row names its place in both files.
Returns: a count, the subfolders, then one line per file: exact file name, title, folder, Dokumentart, page count, topics, the date a photo was taken, a Fassung mark (read from the name, or a replacement a person confirmed, with what changed), upload date, a one-line summary. An index, not a source: it is never cited, and a summary does not say what a file contains. File names are written exactly as returned; each becomes a link the reader can open.

tool:intake:read_document.description: Read a project document's text in full, page by page, under [Seite N] markers, as indexed. At most 12000 characters per call; the answer says when it stopped and which pages to read next. Use it to READ the page a value is on before you record it: a quote you record must stand in text a tool showed you in this run. To FIND which document or page holds a value, use knowledge_search first and then read that page here. Only the project's own documents can be read; the Richtlinien corpus is not a source of project values. An older Fassung says which document replaced it.

file_name.description: The document's exact file name as list_files, intake_needs or a search hit wrote it. Never invented.

pages.description: 1-based page numbers to read, at most 30. Omit to read from the first page on, as far as the bound reaches; the answer names the pages it did not show.

tool:intake:read_passage.description:
Opens a document by name: `document=` alone returns its OUTLINE, the document's opening passage plus a Gliederung of its top-level Punkte, and `document=` with `clause=` or `page=` returns exactly that passage. A lookup, not a search: no ranking, and it cannot find a document from a topic (`knowledge_search` does).
Inputs: `document`, the exact name or display title as the inventory or a hit printed it (e.g. 'OIB-Richtlinie 2, Ausgabe Mai 2023' or 'oib-rl_2_ausgabe_mai_2023.pdf'). `clause`, the number alone ('3.5.2', no 'Pkt.') or a table's caption ('Tabelle 3'), or for a project document what a hit's `Punkt:` line printed ('§ 4', 'Zeilen 2-41'); with `clause=`, `page=` is ignored. `page`, one page number. `pages`, a range ('4-6', at most 30 pages) in reading order without the overlap between neighbouring chunks, up to about 6k tokens; a read that stopped early ends with a `cursor` to pass back with the same `document=`.
Returns: the passages, each with Source, Citation (copy verbatim), Dokumentart, Punkt and page. The Gliederung is an index, not evidence: only passages carry a Citation; a Punkt it lists, or one an outline in a `knowledge_search` result lists, opens here by its number (`clause=`). An unknown document name is refused, with up to three labelled guesses from this turn's readable inventory when anything is close.
`conclusion=` is optional: one line on what you are looking for; it has no effect on the call.

tool:intake:record_values.description: Record values the project's documents state, each with where it stands (citation, or file_name and page) and the verbatim quote that states it. Up to 20 per call, several keys at once. Nothing you record becomes a fact: each value is a suggestion a person confirms against the quote, so record only what a document states for THIS project, as its Zielzustand (a Bestand key: the existing building), never a guess, a typical value or something you worked out. A value the document calls undecided, under review or one of several options is not stated: a person would be confirming a decision nobody made. A drawing's Planart (Einreichplan) names the drawing, not the project's phase. Never record the building class, even where a document states one: the system derives it from the inputs you record and a person confirms it there, so record the inputs the document gives. Value: select, the option token exactly (multi_select: a list); number, a plain number in the question's unit, no unit text (`7,2 m` is 7.2); yes/no, true or false; text, the words as written. Quote: the document's own words, copied from text a tool showed you in this run in that file, at most 300 characters, the sentence, table row or title-block line, never paraphrased or joined from two places. Checked before anything is sent: the quote stands in what you read of that file (when it does not, the answer shows the closest passage you did read), a select value is one of the option tokens and its quote says it. Example: {"values": [{"key": "storeys_above_ground@bldg1", "value": 3, "citation": "Baubeschreibung.pdf, S. 3", "quote": "Das Gebäude hat drei oberirdische Geschoße"}]}. Outcomes, one per value: suggested (new on the profile, a person will check it); corroborated (the profile holds the same value; your evidence was added); contradiction (the profile holds a different value; yours is kept beside it for a person to decide); refused, with the reason and what to do instead. The answer also names the needs your values opened (a building opens its storeys, heights and areas), decisive ones marked: they are needs now, and intake_needs lists them with their options.

values.description: 1 to 20 values, each with its evidence. Several keys in one call.

citation.description: Where the quote stands, as the reading tool printed it: `Baubeschreibung.pdf, p.3` from a search hit, or `Baubeschreibung.pdf, S. 3`. Give this or file_name.

file_name.description: The file the quote stands in, exactly as the reading tool named it.

key.description: The profile key exactly as intake_needs lists it, with its @bldgN (Bauwerk) or @bldgN@use (Nutzungszone) suffix. A key not listed yet is taken when a wizard question writes it (dwelling_units@bldg1@residential before the Nutzungen are recorded).

page.description: The page from the [Seite N] marker or the hit; null if none.

quote.description: The document's own words that state the value, copied verbatim from text a tool showed you in this run, at most 300 characters. Never paraphrased, never assembled from two places.

value.description: The value the document states for THIS project. Select: the option token exactly (multi_select: a list of tokens). Number: a number in the question's unit, no unit text. Boolean: true or false. Text: the words as written.

tool:intake:withdraw_values.description: Take back values you recorded in this run once you see a document does not state them for this project: undecided after all, one of several options, another building's, an older Fassung's. Only your own suggestions from this run can go; a value a person gave or confirmed, the derived building class and an earlier reading's suggestion stay, and the answer says so. A withdrawn value is not refused: no person said no, so a later reading may record it again from a document that states it. To replace a value with another, withdraw it and record the other.

keys.description: 1 to 20 keys, each one you recorded in this run, exactly as recorded.

tool:unbound:describe_card.description: Return the exact JSON shape, the shared building blocks and a worked example for one or more card types, so you can fill `emit_card` in correctly on the first attempt. Pass `card_types`: one type name, or several separated by commas. Call this once for the types you intend to emit; the shapes stay in context afterwards.
